name: TPM Typeface
classification_notes: Built on a 5×7 dot grid with three variable axes controlling dot size, spacing and slant, placing it firmly in the dot matrix display tradition and the broader display category.
summary: A three-axis variable display typeface by Sara Barcons, built on a 5×7 dot grid with axes mapping weight, width and slant to typographic expression.
description: Designed by Sara Barcons, TPM (Types per Minute) originates from an experimental research project in which each variable axis represented a vital sign from a pulse oximetry sensor: dot weight for body temperature, horizontal spacing for oxygen saturation, and slant for heart rate. The typeface comprises eight static styles across light and bold weights in condensed and extended widths, each with italics, plus a variable font covering the full three-axis range. The dot matrix aesthetic makes it well suited to branding, packaging and screen work where a technological or data-driven character is appropriate.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe TPM as a three-axis display variable typeface inspired by early technology displays and based on a 5×7 dot array. The weight axis controls dot size, the width axis adjusts horizontal spacing, and the slant axis tilts the matrix up to 30 degrees. The project emerged from experimental research using a pulse oximetry sensor to represent vital signs in real-time through the variable axes, creating a dual layer of information where letterforms carry data and language carries meaning.

name: 403 Mesapholic
classification_notes: High-contrast sharp serifs in the upright style with a calligraphic, flowing italic that departs substantially from the roman, placing it in the high-contrast serif category with display characteristics.
summary: A two-style display serif with a structured roman and a markedly calligraphic italic, aimed at craft and specialty brand packaging.
description: The upright style carries high contrast and sharp serifs for an editorial, authoritative tone, while the italic departs entirely from the roman into a flowing, calligraphic form intended to read as a personal signature. The duality makes it well suited to logotypes, menus and packaging where a brand wants to alternate between formal confidence and handcrafted warmth. The 501-glyph set includes ligatures, alternates, three numeral sets and extended punctuation.
foundry_blurb: 403 Mesapholic is described by 403TF as a system of two complementary personalities: a high-contrast, razor-sharp Regular for structure and sophistication, and an expressive, fluid Italic that acts as a calligraphic counterpart rather than a simple slant. The foundry positions it as ideal for third-wave coffee roasters, craft distilleries, boutique bakeries and similar artisan brands, particularly for packaging, logotypes and headline use.

name: 403 Sparco
classification_notes: Wide, boxy letterforms with explicit brutalist and industrial utility references place this firmly in display; the Bleed variant's ink-bleed texture and Slant styles confirm it is designed purely for high-impact headline use rather than text setting.
summary: A wide, boxy display typeface in four styles spanning clean machine-cut forms and roughened ink-bleed variants, aimed at techwear, outdoor and brutalist branding.
description: Four styles cover Regular, Slant, Bleed and Bleed Slant, the latter two simulating heavy ink bleed on nylon or weathered signage while the Slant variants add a sense of forward momentum. The letterforms are deliberately wide and structured, suited to oversized headline settings, race bibs, apparel labels and underground event flyers. Each style ships with 769 glyphs including five numeral sets, ligatures, alternates and broad diacritic coverage across 341 languages.
foundry_blurb: 403TF describe 403 Sparco as a heavy-duty display typeface bridging clean digital precision and raw physical grit, rooted in industrial utility and high-performance outdoor gear. The Regular style offers a crisp machine-cut aesthetic, while the Bleed version introduces organic roughness resembling ink bleeding on tactical nylon. With wide, confident and unapologetically boxy proportions, they position it for techwear labels, gorpcore branding, extreme sports apparel and brutalist visual identities.

name: Structur Typeface
classification_notes: A display typeface blending uncial letterforms with cyberpunk and industrial aesthetics; its mix of straight technical lines and rounded curves places it firmly in the display category rather than any classical type genre.
summary: A single-weight display face by Jules Rousseau that fuses uncial manuscript forms with a cyberpunk industrial aesthetic.
description: Straight technical lines meet rounded, fluid curves throughout the 379-glyph character set, producing what the designer calls a mechanical yet neo-medieval hybrid. The Latin European coverage, including diacritics and ligatures, makes it workable across European branding and editorial projects. It sits squarely in high-impact display territory: logos, poster work, underground music identities, and futuristic interface graphics.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe Structur as a typeface that blends uncial and cyberpunk influences, built for a hyper-technological world. They position it for futuristic interface HUDs, experimental posters, and underground music visual identities, citing its 379-glyph set and broad Latin European language support as suited to global branding projects requiring a tech-noir or neo-medieval edge.

name: HV Kanda
classification_notes: A bold, uppercase-only display sans with wide proportions and geometric character, designed explicitly for large-scale, high-impact applications rather than extended text setting.
summary: A single-weight, uppercase display sans by hvnter, built for large-scale branding and poster work with wide proportions and geometric curves.
description: With only 59 glyphs covering uppercase letters, numerals, punctuation and a handful of alternates, HV Kanda is a narrow-purpose display typeface aimed squarely at fashion branding, album covers and social media graphics. Its slightly wide proportions and strong curves give it a confident rhythm at headline sizes, though the limited character set makes it unsuitable for anything beyond short bursts of text. Available in OTF for commercial use, with WOFF and WOFF2 included in the extended licence.
foundry_blurb: HV Kanda is described by the foundry as a bold sans serif built for instant impact, with slightly wide proportions, strong curves and a confident rhythm. Designed for modern and expressive branding, it is said to balance geometric precision with playful character, making it suited to fashion branding, album covers, posters, packaging, social media and contemporary logos.

name: Ultra Mono Typeface
classification_notes: Classified as display due to its experimental constraint-driven design where uppercase and lowercase share identical height, producing a graphic, texture-like typographic surface rather than conventional text use.
summary: A variable display typeface by Maxime Thill built on a single structural rule: uppercase and lowercase characters share identical height, eliminating traditional ascenders and descenders.
description: By forcing all characters to the same vertical measure, Ultra Mono produces dense, compressed text blocks where descenders fold back into the baseline and diacritics sit flush against their letters. The typeface ships as a variable font with adjustable height and slant axes, spanning from a rigid upright to more dynamic angled compositions, with a condensed variant that permits very tight leading. Suited to editorial design, posters and experimental visual identities where typographic density doubles as surface texture.
foundry_blurb: Ultra Mono is described by 6TM Magazine as an experimental display typeface built around a bold typographic constraint: a unified vertical structure where uppercase and lowercase characters share the exact same height. The removal of traditional capital and ascender distinctions creates a dense, compressed rhythm with a contemporary presence. As a variable font with height and slant axes, it supports layouts ranging from rigid and controlled to dynamic and expressive, with a condensed structure enabling extremely tight leading.

name: Inkbleed Light Font
classification_notes: Rooted in grotesque sans-serif logic but heavily distorted through an ink-bleed graphic system, softened edges, and connective ligatures that push it firmly into display/experimental territory.
summary: A single-weight experimental display face by Jeremy Traun that translates the visual effect of ink bleed into a codified graphic system of softened edges and connective ligatures.
description: Built on grotesque sans-serif geometry, Inkbleed Light introduces controlled disruption through rounded terminals, circular alternates, and ligatures that bind numerals, arrows and symbols into continuous typographic forms. A repositioned baseline asterisk signals its intent to challenge conventional typographic hierarchy rather than simply decorate it. The face is listed for inclusion in the Yearbook of Type 2026 and is aimed at bold brand identities where visual friction is the point.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe Inkbleed Light as an experimental display font that brings geometric clarity into tension with controlled disruption, inspired by grotesque sans-serif logic and translating ink bleed into a graphic system of softened edges, circular alternates, and connective ligatures. Numerals, arrows and symbols merge into continuous typographic forms, while a repositioned baseline asterisk challenges default hierarchies.

name: dclt Typeface
classification_notes: A variable pixel display typeface built around strict pixel grids; its four styles (dot, chip, line, tape) span compact square pixels to wide flat strokes, firmly placing it in the display/pixel category.
summary: A variable pixel display typeface in four distinct styles, from dense dot grids to tall narrow tape bars, built for experimental and glitch-influenced work.
description: Four styles, dot, chip, line and tape, each bring a different visual rhythm ranging from compact square pixels to wide flat strokes and stretched vertical bars. Variable technology gives designers flexibility across layouts, and the family is explicitly designed to be pushed beyond conventional use: stacked, outlined, glitched or distorted. With 305 glyphs including diacritics, alternates and mathematical symbols, it covers the practical needs of posters, album artwork, motion design and digital interfaces.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe dclt as a variable pixel display typeface whose four styles move between strict pixel grids and more expressive forms. Designed by Guillaume Santial to be misused, it is positioned for experimental and contemporary design projects that embrace glitch aesthetics and bold visual identity, including posters, branding, album artwork and motion design.

name: GEO Typeface
classification_notes: GEO is a display typeface with heavily textured, stone-like letterforms built for high-impact use at large sizes; its extreme visual complexity and geological inspiration place it firmly in the experimental display category.
summary: An experimental all-caps display typeface by Lena Weber, built from around 20,000 anchors per glyph to simulate the physical complexity of geological stone samples.
description: Each glyph carries approximately 20,000 anchors, creating a dense, stone-like texture that pushes the limits of what a digital typeface can encode. The family ships with two to four contextual alternates per letter, activated automatically via OpenType features to prevent repetition across a composition. Best suited to posters, album artwork and editorial layouts where it can be set large enough for the detail to read.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe GEO as an experimental typeface that explores the maximum texture a typeface can store, with each glyph's physical complexity drawn from geological samples. They note that no two stones are alike, so the font includes 2–4 alternates per letter activated via contextual OpenType features, producing natural variation and an organic feel suited to expressive, high-impact typography.

name: Abyme Typeface
classification_notes: A self-referential, layered display typeface built for maximalist and experimental graphic use, with no conventional text application intended.
summary: A self-referential display typeface by Maxime Thill built on the mise en abyme concept, offering three weight styles suited to maximalist and experimental graphic work.
description: Derived from the ÆUROPA Typeface, Abyme uses a layered, self-referential structure to create bold, graphic letterforms across three styles: ×111, ×222, and ×333. Each weight pushes the visual density further, moving from sharp contrast to immersive, dense compositions. The 81-glyph set is aimed at editorial layouts, ASCII projects, branding and contemporary visual identities.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe Abyme as inspired by the mise en abyme concept, a technique in which a work contains a smaller version or reflection of itself. Version 2.0 introduced three distinct weight styles (×111, ×222, ×333) to expand it into a more versatile visual system. They position it for ASCII projects, editorial layouts, branding and experimental design, noting that its layered forms feel both graphic and conceptual.

name: 403 Super Vega
classification_notes: Monolinear strokes, rounded geometric letterforms and a futuristic aesthetic place this firmly in the geometric display category, designed for large-scale titles and headings rather than continuous text.
summary: A monolinear geometric display face from 403TF with rounded letterforms and a sci-fi flavour suited to titles and logos.
description: Built on thin, monolinear strokes and rounded balanced letterforms, it aims for a crisp contemporary feel with minor idiosyncrasies in letters such as 'k', 'y' and 'g'. The family ships in two styles, Regular and Slant, with 496 glyphs covering diacritics, ligatures, alternates, currency and mathematical symbols. It is oriented towards editorial headlines, tech branding and experimental design work at large sizes.
foundry_blurb: 403TF describe Super Vega as a sleek, contemporary font with a geometric and futuristic look suited to the creative, tech and sci-fi sectors. They highlight its rounded letterforms and thin monolinear strokes as giving it a crisp, modern appearance, with distinctive details in certain letters adding individuality. The font is positioned for editorial titles, headings and logos, and is aimed at forward-thinking brands and experimental design projects.

name: 403 Obrinda
classification_notes: A fixed-width typeface with prominent serifs and a typewriter heritage, placing it squarely in the monospaced slab serif subcategory rather than a purely utilitarian mono.
summary: A slab-serif monospaced typeface drawing on typewriter heritage, available in five weights with matching slanted variants and variable font technology.
description: Built on a fixed-width grid with confident serifs and balanced proportions, 403 Obrinda takes its cues from the mechanical clarity of typewriter type while keeping its forms clean enough for screen and editorial use. The family spans five weights from Light to Black, each with a slanted companion, and ships as a variable font covering 602 glyphs including ligatures, alternates, mathematical symbols and currency signs. Suited to branding, data-heavy interfaces, dashboards and editorial layouts where a structured rhythm and legibility are both required.
foundry_blurb: 403TF describe 403 Obrinda as a monospaced typeface where mechanical precision and humanistic warmth meet, framed as a tribute to the golden age of typewriters reimagined for digital use. They position it as a workhorse for branding agencies, editorial designers and UI/UX practitioners, noting its deliberate structure as purposeful rather than restrictive, and highlight its 10 styles, variable technology and 602-glyph character set.

name: Rocaille Typeface
classification_notes: The foundry explicitly describes Rocaille as a Slab Mono, combining monospaced letterforms with slab serif construction and geometric shapes inspired by natural stone.
summary: A slab monospaced typeface by Jules Rousseau that replaces conventional screen-optimised slab forms with angular, stone-like organic shapes.
description: Designed by Jules Rousseau, Rocaille draws a conceptual line between the digital language of code and the physical language of rock climbing, treating both as systems of communication between human and environment. The geometric construction departs from the smooth, screen-friendly conventions of most slab serifs, favouring rougher, more mineral forms. It covers 342 glyphs across Latin European, including diacritics, ligatures, mathematics and currency symbols.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe Rocaille as a Slab Mono with geometric shapes inspired by rocks and mountains. The design deconstructs conventional slab forms, typically built for screens, to propose organic shapes drawn from natural stone, drawing a parallel between the digital world of code and the physical pursuit of rock climbing as two distinct modes of communication.

name: Bezier Typeface
classification_notes: Bezier is a mono-modular display typeface built on a tiling grid system where all non-connector strokes are smooth curves, placing it firmly in the experimental/display category rather than any conventional serif or sans classification.
summary: A mono-modular tiling typeface by Lena Weber in which all letterforms are built from smooth curves, allowing them to interlock horizontally and vertically without spacing to form continuous pattern-like compositions.
description: Designed by Lena Weber, Bezier operates as a typographic tiling system where uppercase letters and numerals share a common module footprint, enabling them to butt together on a grid without gaps. Every non-connector line is a smooth Bézier curve, giving compositions a fluid, almost liquid quality despite sitting on a strict geometric structure. The 36-glyph set is intentionally limited, aimed at poster work, bold branding and experimental layout rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe Bezier as a typographic tiling system whose mono-modular design lets letters flow together horizontally and vertically with zero spacing, producing freeform and liquid-looking compositions that simultaneously build a perfect grid. All non-connector lines are smooth curves, making it suited to generative design, typographic patterns, posters, branding and digital design.

name: Normal TM
classification_notes: Described as a sans serif with contextual alternates and stylistic sets producing organic variation; no further structural detail places it beyond a general grotesque classification.
summary: A single-weight sans serif with two stylistic sets and contextual alternates that rotate automatically to give layouts an organic, varied feel.
description: Designed by Type Mania, Normal TM uses contextual alternatives and two stylistic sets to shuffle glyph variants without manual intervention, keeping text from looking mechanically uniform. The 270-glyph set covers upper and lowercase, diacritics, ligatures, numbers, punctuation, currency and mathematics. Available in OTF and TTF for commercial use, with WOFF2 added in the extended licence.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe Normal TM as a gently handled sans serif that rotates two stylistic sets with contextual alternatives active, making layouts look organic and almost automatic in their variation.

name: Junky Notes
classification_notes: Junky Notes is a casual handwritten script designed to mimic notebook scribbles, doodles and margin sketches, placing it firmly in the informal handwritten subcategory of script typefaces.
summary: A casual handwritten typeface by Softulka, built around the irregular strokes and uneven spacing of notebook margins and everyday pen scribbles.
description: Two weights, Regular and Bold, make up this 192-glyph script designed to mimic the spontaneous energy of doodles and quick sketches rather than polished calligraphy. Its deliberately imperfect rhythm and hand-drawn character give it an approachable warmth suited to posters, greeting cards, packaging and children's projects. Diacritics, currency symbols and basic mathematics are included, broadening its utility beyond decorative use.
foundry_blurb: Junky Notes is described by the foundry as a playful handwritten typeface inspired by the imperfect beauty of notebook margins, quick sketches, spontaneous doodles and everyday pen scribbles. They say it celebrates authenticity over polish, with a loose rhythm and hand-drawn character that makes it feel pulled directly from a creative journal or sketchbook.

name: OFW Helvet
classification_notes: Based on Helvetica Bold letterforms with a recurring Off-White cross pattern overlaid, making it a decorative or display variant rather than a functional text typeface.
summary: A single-weight decorative typeface based on Helvetica Bold, overlaid with the Off-White cross motif as a tribute to Virgil Abloh.
description: Designed by ENCH as a personal homage to Virgil Abloh, the letterforms derive directly from Helvetica Bold, a typeface closely associated with Abloh's visual identity at Off-White. The Off-White cross pattern is woven into the design as a recurring decorative element, referencing Abloh's signature graphic language. The family covers 81 glyphs including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, punctuation and symbols, available in OTF and TTF formats.
foundry_blurb: ENCH describes OFW Helvet as a tribute to Virgil Abloh, built on Helvetica Bold letterforms and incorporating the iconic Off-White cross as a recurring visual pattern. Developed through a long and careful design process, it is presented as a personal homage to a major creative influence.

name: Dukat Typeface
classification_notes: An experimental display typeface with variable optical sizes simulating the progressive decay of vinyl lettering, inspired by decorative Ukrainian manuscript script; clearly display-oriented with no text applications implied.
summary: An experimental variable display typeface by Alyona Korysta that stages the progressive decay of vinyl letterforms across five optical styles, rooted in Ukrainian manuscript script tradition.
description: Each of the five styles — numbered 12 through 96 — represents a stage in the physical deterioration of a vinyl letter, from intact to near-abstract, while each character holds a fixed width across all stages. The concept draws equally from Vyaz, the ornamental ligature script found in historic Ukrainian manuscripts, and from the weathered aesthetic of peeling adhesive signage. Latin and Cyrillic coverage spans Ukrainian, Serbian and Macedonian, with 544 glyphs including ligatures, alternates and a variable font file.
foundry_blurb: Dukat is described by 6TM Magazine as an experimental display typeface inspired by the modularity and decorativeness of Vyaz, a historic decorative script used in Ukrainian manuscripts, and by weathered vinyl signage that slowly peels and turns letterforms abstract and ornamental. Each style keeps its letters at the same width, reflecting how a real vinyl letter might look at the start of its life and how destructured it becomes over time.

name: sMegs Display
classification_notes: Explicitly described as a bold display typeface with hand-drawn character and rough, organic letterforms, placing it squarely in the display category with a hand-drawn subcategory.
summary: A bold, hand-drawn display typeface with textured, organic letterforms offered in two raw styles for posters and distinctive branding.
description: Designed by hvnter, sMegs Display leans on rough edges and tactile, hand-drawn shapes to bring personality to large-scale typographic work. Two styles are included within the 213-glyph set, covering uppercase, lowercase, alternates, numbers and basic punctuation. Aimed at posters, album covers and branding where a raw, expressive quality is required.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe sMegs Display as a bold display typeface with hand-drawn character and strong, organic letterforms, noting that its textured shapes and slightly rough edges bring depth and personality to typography. They highlight its two raw styles as offering flexibility while maintaining a consistent, expressive look, and position it for posters, album covers and distinctive branding.

name: Late Cinema Handwritten Script
classification_notes: Categorised as script due to its handwritten character throughout, with the designer noting a deliberate blend of sans-serif structure in the uppercase and flowing script in the lowercase.
summary: A handwritten script by Victoria Strukovskaya that pairs bold, confident uppercase letters with a flowing lowercase to balance structure with a personal, informal quality.
description: The uppercase characters carry the weight of a strong sans-serif, making them serviceable for headlines and logos, while the lowercase shifts into a natural handwritten rhythm that softens the overall feel. With 199 glyphs covering Latin European characters, diacritics, numbers, currency and mathematics, it covers practical range for branding and packaging work. Available in OTF and TTF under commercial licence, with web formats added at the extended tier.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe Late Cinema as a versatile handwritten font that blends the boldness of a strong sans-serif with the warmth of a handwritten script. The uppercase is intended for headlines, logos and titles, while the lowercase adds intimacy and natural rhythm. They position it for branding, posters, packaging and projects that need both impact and subtle emotion, with support for the most popular Latin-based languages.

name: MOB-X3
classification_notes: Condensed, heavy and angular letterforms with a futuristic aesthetic place this firmly in the display category; the tight geometry and sharp construction recall sci-fi and electronic music visual culture rather than any classical type tradition.
summary: A condensed, angular display face by Jules Bigot, originating from experimental electronic music visuals and built around a stark, futuristic aesthetic.
description: Designed initially for electronic music contexts, the face carries condensed proportions and heavy, angular letterforms that read strongly at large sizes while remaining functional in editorial settings. Version 1.0 ships as a single Regular style with a Latin European character set covering over 370 glyphs, including alternates, three numeral sets, arrows and mathematical symbols. The extended licence adds WOFF and WOFF2 formats for web use.
foundry_blurb: 6TM describe MOB-X3 as an entity rooted in their server systems and spreading through contemporary digital culture, originally created for experimental electronic music before evolving into a complete futuristic typeface for bold visual communication across branding, posters, editorial layouts and digital projects.

name: Kodai Typeface
classification_notes: Kodai is explicitly a display typeface built on an italic axis with handwritten influences translated into angular, high-contrast letterforms, placing it firmly in the display category with script-derived characteristics.
summary: A single-weight display typeface by Sinuhé Cid that translates handwritten energy into sharp, angular letterforms set on a strong italic axis.
description: Designed by Sinuhé Cid, Kodai takes the gestural rhythm of handwriting and refines it into a bold, angular display face with contrasting strokes and a pronounced forward lean. The 231-glyph Latin European character set covers diacritics, ligatures, currency and mathematical symbols, making it reasonably complete for its intended uses. It suits headline work, editorial layouts and visual identity projects where momentum and personality are the priority.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe Kodai as a dynamic display typeface that combines expressive, handwritten influences with a sharp, angular design. Built on a strong italic axis, it captures the energy of handwritten gestures and translates them into sharp forms that give each word a sense of forward momentum, making it particularly suited to headlines, editorial layouts, visual identities and expressive typographic compositions.

name: Mother TM
classification_notes: An organic display face with ink bleeds and hand-drawn character, designed for expressive headline use rather than continuous text. Two alternating stylistic sets reinforce its informal, craft-inflected nature.
summary: An organic hand-drawn display face with ink bleeds and two contextual stylistic sets that alternate automatically as you type.
description: Drawn with visible ink bleed and hand-crafted irregularity, this display face from Type Mania leans into texture and spontaneity. Contextual Alternates cycle between two distinct stylistic sets automatically, introducing rhythm and variation without manual intervention. With 249 glyphs covering Latin diacritics, numbers, punctuation and currency, it covers most Latin-based language needs for headline and expressive typographic work.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe Mother TM as an organic display typeface with ink bleeds and hand-drawn character. Activating Contextual Alternates causes the face to rotate between two stylistic sets as you type. It supports the most popular Latin-based languages and ships in OTF and TTF formats under commercial licensing, with WOFF2 added on extended licences.

name: UNKNOWN Typeface
classification_notes: The typeface is built from a linear grid system with organic character variation across three stylistic cuts, placing it firmly in the geometric display category.
summary: A grid-derived display typeface in three stylistic cuts — RND, PX and MX — with organic character variation and extensive alternate glyphs.
description: Designed by Lukas Haider and Alexander Raffl, UNKNOWN draws its structure from a linear grid system while introducing enough variation across individual characters to keep the overall texture feeling organic rather than mechanical. Three distinct styles — RND, PX and MX — give designers flexibility, with additional alternates accessible via uppercase and lowercase switching. At 375 glyphs, it covers diacritics, symbols, currency and mathematics, making it well suited to editorial, artwork and identity projects.
foundry_blurb: 6TM Magazine describe UNKNOWN as a contemporary display typeface by Lukas Haider and Alexander Raffl, comprising three styles — RND, PX and MX — rooted in a linear grid system yet remaining organic through character variation. With 375 glyphs including alternates, diacritics and symbols, they position it as ideal for artworks, magazines and logos.

name: Niche Things
classification_notes: Single-weight casual handwritten script with intentional irregularity. Curved, carefree letterforms with deliberate unevenness in rhythm and movement. No variants or subfamilies. Covers 197 glyphs including uppercase, lowercase, diacritics, numbers, punctuation and currency symbols.
summary: A single-weight casual handwritten script with deliberate unevenness and curvy letterforms, aimed at youthful branding, packaging and editorial work that needs a spontaneous, human feel.
description: Niche Things is a bold handwritten script by designer Victoria Strukovskaya, built around irregular rhythm and curved, raw letterforms. The 197-glyph set covers uppercase, lowercase, diacritics and common symbols, supporting most Latin-based languages. It suits trend-led visual work: packaging, social media graphics, apparel and branding that calls for a handmade aesthetic.
foundry_blurb: A font that pairs playful energy with a slightly raw, unpolished quality. Its curved shapes and uneven movement give it a spontaneous, human-centred character suited to posters, packaging, product labels, social media graphics and apparel. Available in OTF and TTF under commercial or extended licence, with WOFF/WOFF2 on the extended tier.

name: Tokyoto Typeface
classification_notes: Modular uppercase-only display typeface where every letter is constructed from a repeating hook-shaped unit; five style variants differ only in the treatment of the connecting knot element rather than in weight or width.
summary: A modular display typeface built from a single hook-shaped unit, offered in five decorative style variants drawn from Japanese visual culture.
description: Tokyoto builds every glyph from one repeating hook module that links to its neighbours, producing letterforms with an architectural, near-hieroglyphic quality. Five styles – Dott, Bubble, Point, Roll and Flower – share the same geometric skeleton but treat the connecting knot differently, ranging from fine dots to bubbled and floral textures. The uppercase-only character set (64 glyphs per style) makes it best suited to headlines, branding and poster work rather than body copy.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by ukiyo-e prints, temple ornaments and the signage of Tokyo and Kyoto, each letter is assembled from a single hook-shaped module that interlocks with its neighbours. The five style variants – Dott, Bubble, Point, Roll and Flower – vary the knot that ties modules together. Every style ships with uppercase letters, numerals, punctuation, arrows and a bonus emoji set; licences include OTF and TTF, with WOFF and WOFF2 added in the extended tier.

name: StarForm
classification_notes: Experimental modular display face constructed from a single four-point geometric unit repeated across all characters; letterforms blur into pattern and symbol, designed for maximum graphic impact at large sizes. No italic, condensed or mono variants.
summary: A modular geometric display face built on a four-point grid, turning every character into a graphic composition of rhythm, symmetry and negative space.
description: StarForm is an experimental display face by Softulka, constructed from a single repeating geometric module on a strict grid. Each character sits at the boundary between letterform, symbol and pattern, lending itself to poster headers, album artwork and graphic identity work that needs strong visual density. It ships in OTF, TTF and WOFF with 193 glyphs and full diacritical support.
foundry_blurb: The listing positions StarForm as a typeface that turns words into striking graphic compositions built from rhythm, symmetry and negative space. Pitched at experimental editorial design, futuristic branding, gallery posters, logo work, exhibition graphics and motion design, each character follows a precise four-point modular grid that blurs the line between typography and pattern.

name: Quiet Wild Whimsical Floral Script
classification_notes: Single-weight handwritten script with organic, flowing letterforms and botanical floral embellishments. Designed in a whimsical, artisan style typical of indie calligraphy fonts aimed at wedding and lifestyle branding markets.
summary: A single-weight handwritten script with floral embellishments and an organic character, aimed at botanical branding, wedding stationery and lifestyle packaging.
description: Quiet Wild draws on wildflower meadows and the texture of imperfect, hand-drawn lettering, with decorative floral details woven through the letterforms. Its 197-glyph character set covers Latin European diacritics alongside numerals, punctuation and currency symbols. Available in OTF and TTF under a commercial licence, with web formats (WOFF, WOFF2) at an extended tier.
foundry_blurb: A whimsical handwritten script inspired by hidden meadows and wildflowers, featuring delicate floral character details and full Latin European diacritics. Sold with commercial and extended licence options, each including OTF and TTF files.

name: Weird Horses
classification_notes: Single-weight hand-drawn display face with irregular letterforms, uneven strokes and a raw sketchbook aesthetic. No constructed or geometric logic – the design is entirely driven by expressive, loose mark-making. 369 glyphs with two stylistic sets and alternates give some variation within the one weight.
summary: A single-weight hand-drawn display face from The Native Saint Club, built around raw irregular letterforms and deliberate sketchbook energy aimed at gig posters and streetwear graphics.
description: Weird Horses leans into imperfection as its main feature – bold strokes, uneven letter construction and forms that read as pulled from a wall rather than assembled on a grid. At 369 glyphs it covers uppercase letters, diacritics, numerals, punctuation, currency and maths symbols, with two stylistic sets and alternates providing some variation within the single weight. The target contexts are deliberately narrow: gig posters, merch graphics and music visuals where handmade texture is the point.
foundry_blurb: The 6TM listing describes Weird Horses as a raw underground display face that resists refinement, with characters carrying bold strokes and irregular energy drawn from sketchbook and street-culture sources. Intended for gig posters, merchandise graphics, music visuals and streetwear branding.

name: Nolune
classification_notes: Single-weight blackletter-derived display script with organic detailing – hooked terminals, variable stroke weights that shift between razor sharpness and rough erosion. 61 glyphs covering uppercase and lowercase Latin only. Clearly a display-only face; not suited to body text.
summary: A single-weight blackletter display script by Alex Ortiga, designed for dark fantasy use – game titles, album art and occult packaging – with hooked terminals and deliberately eroded stroke weights.
description: Nolune draws on blackletter tradition and layers in organic extensions, hooked terminals and stroke weights that shift between sharp precision and rough decay. It was developed alongside an unreleased dark fantasy tabletop RPG rooted in Northern Italian folklore, and that specificity of origin shows in the letterforms. With 61 glyphs and one style, its range is narrow: atmospheric display work only.
foundry_blurb: Nolune is a dark fantasy display script born from an unreleased tabletop RPG set in Northern Italian rural mythology. The letterforms balance blackletter structure with organic collapse – hooked terminals, shifting stroke weights and raw erosion create a tension between precision and decay. Available as OTF for commercial use, with WOFF and WOFF2 included on the extended licence.

name: Konsumed
classification_notes: Geometric display sans-serif built around a seven-width axis (Compressed through Extended) with a parallel Blurred set as a second stylistic subfamily. No italic or bold variants. Uppercase and lowercase with diacritics, ligatures and five numeral sets.
summary: A display sans-serif built across seven widths from compressed to extended, with a matching blurred set for soft-focus typographic effects in high-impact work.
description: Konsumed pairs seven width variants – Compressed through Extended – with matching blurred counterparts, giving designers 14 styles within one coherent system. The blurred subfamily is designed for soft-focus transitions within the same type family, suited to posters, sports graphics and editorial work where type carries visual weight. With 518 glyphs, diacritics and five numeral sets, it has reasonable coverage across Latin extended languages.
foundry_blurb: A display sans serif designed for expressive, high-impact visual work, pairing regular and blurred styles to enable transitions from sharp to soft-focus typography within the same family. A flexible width spectrum runs from compressed to extended, covering branding, packaging, editorial and digital applications. Available under commercial and extended licences.

name: Blurline Utility Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight display face constructed from horizontal scan lines with softened edges and deliberate ink bleed. The effect evokes aged print, scanned documents and weathered information systems. Anti-design sensibility drawing on industrial signage and technical documentation.
summary: A single-weight industrial display face built from scan-line texture and ink bleed, suited to posters, album artwork and experimental editorial.
description: Blurline merges mechanical precision with analog imperfection, its letterforms constructed from horizontal scan lines, softened edges and deliberate ink bleed. The aesthetic draws on industrial signage and technical documentation, landing somewhere between aged print and contemporary anti-design. At its best in large-scale, display-only contexts: posters, packaging, album artwork and motion graphics where tactile texture is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Blurline is built from imperfect horizontal scan lines, softened edges and subtle ink bleed, drawing on industrial signage, anti-design aesthetics and technical documentation. The result merges mechanical precision with analog character across 194 glyphs covering uppercase, lowercase, diacritics, numbers, punctuation, symbols, currency and mathematical characters. Licensed in OTF and TTF formats for commercial and extended use.

name: Bodark
classification_notes: Hand-drawn display typeface rooted in spray-paint graffiti and urban tagging culture. Two variants – Clean and Spray – sit at different points on the rawness spectrum. No italic, condensed, or mono styles. Primarily uppercase with diacritics suggesting extended Latin coverage. 369 glyphs including alternates, numbers, punctuation and currency.
summary: A hand-drawn graffiti display typeface in two spray-paint variants – Clean and Spray – built for streetwear, posters and bold editorial work.
description: Bodark is a display typeface by The Native Saint Club, drawing directly from raw spray-paint tagging culture. Two variants offer different levels of finish: Clean pulls back the chaos into controlled edges, while Spray lets the overspray read. The 369-glyph set covers uppercase, alternates, diacritics and currency, giving designers enough flexibility within its narrow street-art brief.
foundry_blurb: Bodark channels the organic unpredictability of spray-paint graffiti into a display font suited to posters, streetwear branding, album covers and social media layouts. Two variants – Clean and Spray – let designers dial in how raw the finish feels, with no two characters rendered identically for an authentic tagging aesthetic.

name: Borde
classification_notes: Wide geometric sans serif with brutalist inflections; confrontational optical weight even in lighter cuts; no humanist softening; confident proportions derived from raw architectural references rather than classical type models
summary: A five-weight brutalist sans serif drawing on raw architectural forms, with genuine optical range from Light to Black.
description: Borde takes its cues from concrete, steel and exposed structure, producing a sans serif with confrontational presence and confident proportions. Five weights from Light to Black give it real range across editorial and branding work, and a 498-glyph set includes diacritics, alternates and five numeral styles. No italic or condensed variants exist, which suits its single-minded architectural character.
foundry_blurb: A bold brutalist sans serif built to make an immediate impact. Inspired by raw architectural forms, it channels the visual weight of concrete, steel and exposed structure into a typeface that is as confrontational as it is legible. Available in five weights with multilingual support and OTF, TTF, WOFF and WOFF2 formats across commercial and extended licences.

name: Estetika Maison
classification_notes: High-contrast modern serif with retro/nostalgic influences; four styles including Regular, Italic and a distressed "Ruged" variant; 641 glyphs with diacritics, ligatures and multiple numeral sets; broadly in the editorial/contemporary serif tradition with didone-adjacent contrast levels.
summary: A high-contrast contemporary serif with expressive italics and a textured "Ruged" variant, designed for editorial layouts and luxury brand applications.
description: Estetika Maison draws on retro aesthetic references while maintaining clean, contemporary proportions. Four styles – Regular, Italic, Ruged and Ruged Italic – cover standard editorial needs alongside a rougher, distressed variant. With 641 glyphs including multiple numeral sets, ligatures and diacritics, it is well-equipped for magazine layouts, packaging and logo work.
foundry_blurb: A contemporary serif typeface inspired by retro aesthetic trends, featuring strong contrast, refined details and expressive italics. Described as carrying a nostalgic character that stays clean and elegant, it is pitched at editorial text, luxury branding, magazine layouts, packaging and logo design. Available in OTF, TTF and web formats under commercial and extended licences.

name: Sunnie TM
classification_notes: Single-weight casual handwritten script with a Y2K aesthetic. Uses OpenType contextual alternates to cycle automatically through three stylistic sets, simulating natural handwriting variation. No italic, condensed or mono variants. Display use only.
summary: A single-weight Y2K handwritten script that uses contextual alternates to rotate automatically through three stylistic sets, lending the text a more organic, uneven rhythm.
description: Sunnie TM is a loose, scribbled script designed for display use, built around three stylistic sets that cycle via contextual alternates to break up repetition without manual intervention. The Y2K-leaning aesthetic suits casual branding, social graphics and editorial headlines where imperfection is the point. It ships in a single weight with 325 glyphs covering Latin-based languages.
foundry_blurb: Described by its creator as "a loose scribble that rotates three stylistic sets automatically with the contextual alternates fired up," giving designers a more natural rhythm straight out of the box. Includes lowercase, uppercase, diacritics, numbers, punctuation and currency symbols. Available as OTF and TTF under commercial and extended licences.

name: Fever Dream
classification_notes: The product page titles it "Fever Dream – Surreal Handwritten Display Font". It is a sans-serif/script hybrid: bold, structured uppercase characters paired with handwritten-style lowercase. The explicit "display font" designation and headline/branding positioning places it in the display category rather than script.
summary: A single-weight handwritten display face that pairs bold, structured uppercase letterforms with looser script-style lowercase, aimed at headlines, packaging and branding.
description: Fever Dream is a display font by Victoria Strukovskaya that places heavy sans-serif capitals alongside handwritten lowercase characters, creating a deliberate contrast between structure and spontaneity. The 197-glyph set covers Latin European languages including diacritics, numerals and punctuation. It is positioned for posters, packaging, logos and editorial headlines where a rough-edged warmth is the point.
foundry_blurb: The listing describes it as blending the boldness of a strong sans-serif with the warmth and personality of a handwritten script, positioning it as a versatile choice for branding, posters and packaging where structural impact and emotional depth are both required.

name: ÆUROPA
classification_notes: Geometric condensed sans-serif. The condensed proportion is intrinsic to the design concept rather than a variant within a wider family. Clean, upright construction with a focus on European diacritic coverage.
summary: A single-weight geometric condensed sans-serif by Maxime Thill, built around European linguistic diversity with 223 glyphs and broad diacritic coverage.
description: ÆUROPA is a geometric condensed sans-serif designed by Maxime Thill, taking its concept from the many languages and accents of Europe. The character set runs to 223 glyphs, covering uppercase, lowercase, numerals, punctuation, currency, arrows, mathematical symbols and a wide range of Latin diacritics. It ships in OTF, TTF and web formats, making it serviceable for display work in multilingual contexts, though the single weight limits its versatility.
foundry_blurb: A modern geometric condensed typeface inspired by the diversity of Europe's languages and their many accents, reflecting European cultural richness through clean, simple forms.

name: Den Display
classification_notes: Bold futuristic display typeface with Y2K aesthetic. Single weight; uppercase only (A–Z) with multiple alternate characters; 146 glyphs total. No italic, condensed, or mono variants.
summary: A single-weight Y2K display face with futuristic letterforms and alternate characters, built for poster and logo work.
description: Den Display is a bold, futuristic display typeface with a Y2K sensibility, designed for titles, posters and custom wordmarks. Its 146-glyph set covers uppercase letters, numerals and basic punctuation, with multiple alternate characters for compositional variation. Available as a single OTF weight with no italic or condensed cuts.
foundry_blurb: A bold Y2K-inspired display typeface designed to bring energy and individuality to typography, featuring futuristic letterforms and multiple alternate characters across a 146-glyph set.

name: Overprint TM
classification_notes: Distressed sans-serif display typeface with a xeroxed or photocopied aesthetic. Letterforms have deliberately rough, uneven edges. Two stylistic sets alternate automatically via contextual alternates to avoid mechanical repetition of degraded letterforms.
summary: A single-weight distressed display sans built around a deliberately degraded, photocopied texture, with contextual alternates that cycle two stylistic sets to keep letterforms feeling organic rather than mechanical.
description: Overprint TM is a distressed display typeface by Type Mania, designed around a xeroxed, photocopied aesthetic with rough and uneven edges. Two stylistic sets alternate automatically through contextual alternates, giving words a hand-worn quality rather than mechanical repetition. Coverage reaches 253 glyphs across Latin-based languages, including diacritics, ligatures and standard typographic characters; a companion outline variant is sold separately as Overprint Outline TM.
foundry_blurb: Overprint TM is a distressed sans-serif display font with uneven edges and a xeroxed finish. Two stylistic sets automatically alternate via contextual alternates, introducing subtle imperfections across words. The 253-glyph set covers diacritics, ligatures, alternates, numbers, punctuation, symbols and currency characters, with support for most popular Latin-based languages.

name: Dotted Ink Font
classification_notes: Display typeface with medieval calligraphy roots, reimagined through dotted structures and circular geometry rather than traditional pen strokes. Single-weight release with a strong novelty character; adjacent to the blackletter tradition in inspiration but constructed via dots and procedural-inspired forms.
summary: A single-weight display typeface that reimagines medieval calligraphy through dotted structures and circular geometry, suited to atmospheric headlines and fantasy branding.
description: Dotted Ink draws on illuminated manuscript traditions and translates them into a system of dots, circular motifs and procedural geometry. Designed by Iuliia Mazur under the Softulka name, it blends historical lettering with digital experimentation. The 192-glyph set covers Latin diacritics, making it workable across Western European languages for editorial, packaging and identity work where ornament is the point.
foundry_blurb: A decorative display typeface that reimagines historical calligraphy through a contemporary digital lens. Draws on hand-placed ink marks, decorative script traditions, ASCII art and generative graphics to create letterforms described as timeless yet unconventional. The 192-glyph set covers uppercase, lowercase, diacritics, numerals, punctuation and currency characters. Available in OTF and TTF under a commercial licence, with WOFF added at extended licence tier.

name: Gym Mat Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight uppercase-only display face with letterforms derived from the interlocking puzzle-edge curves of foam gym mats. Highly decorative and tactile. Very limited glyph set of 27 characters; not suited to body copy or extended setting.
summary: A single-weight uppercase display face by Maxime Thill, with each letterform traced from the interlocking puzzle-edge curves of foam gym mats.
description: Gym Mat is a bold display typeface built from the chunky, interlocking geometry of classic foam exercise mats. Each letterform traces the puzzle-edge curves of the material, giving the face a sturdy, tactile quality well suited to posters and sports-themed titles. The character set is uppercase-only with just 27 glyphs, so its application is strictly display.
foundry_blurb: A bold display typeface with letterforms traced directly from the chunky, puzzle-edge curves of foam gym mats. The result is a sturdy, detailed and tactile uppercase set with a huge, energetic presence designed for titles and posters.

name: Surfo
classification_notes: Single-weight display typeface with a handmade paper-cut aesthetic. Chunky, irregular letterforms evoke vintage beach signage and hand-scissored paper lettering. Ships with a companion tropical dingbat set (Surfo Dingbat). No condensed, italic or mono variants noted.
summary: A chunky cutout display typeface from The Native Saint Club, built on the imperfect geometry of hand-scissored paper lettering and vintage beach signage.
description: Surfo's letterforms carry the wobble and irregularity of paper mock-ups and hand-painted surf signs – intentionally imperfect, friendly without tipping into childish. The text family covers 475 glyphs, including diacritics, three numeral sets, punctuation, symbols and currency. A companion set of 54 tropical dingbats rounds out the release for decorative headline and poster work.
foundry_blurb: Surfo is a cutout display font inspired by vintage beach signage and handmade paper lettering, with chunky organic shapes, imperfect cuts and a handcrafted construction with intentional human-touch irregularity. The full family includes Surfo Text (475 glyphs) and Surfo Dingbat (54 tropical icons), available in OTF/TTF under commercial or extended licence.

name: Overprint Outline TM
classification_notes: Outline cut of a distressed grungy sans-serif. Uneven, broken stroke edges mimic repeated photocopier passes. Two stylistic sets engage automatically via contextual alternates to cycle imperfections, so no two words render identically. Purely a display face; unsuitable at text sizes.
summary: The outline cut of Type Mania's Overprint TM, a xerox-distressed display face that uses contextual alternates to rotate two stylistic sets and simulate worn, imperfect type.
description: Overprint Outline TM is a grungy display face built to look like text run repeatedly through a photocopier. Its broken, uneven stroke edges are reinforced by two stylistic sets that cycle automatically via contextual alternates, so each word carries slightly different imperfections. Suited to lo-fi logotypes, editorial headers and social media graphics with a grunge or Y2K sensibility.
foundry_blurb: A distressed, xerox-style outline display typeface with 253 glyphs and intentionally uneven edges. Two built-in stylistic sets rotate through contextual alternates to introduce subtle variation across words. Supplied in OTF, TTF and WOFF2; covers most popular Latin-based languages including Central European and Pan African Latin scripts.

name: Giant's Typeface
classification_notes: Two-style geometric display typeface inspired by the hexagonal basalt formations at Giant's Causeway, Ireland. Regular style is bold and rugged; Angle style is smoother and more refined. No italic, condensed or monospace variants. 158 glyphs covering basic Latin characters, numerals and punctuation.
summary: A bold geometric display face by Maxime Thill, drawn from the hexagonal basalt columns of Ireland's Giant's Causeway, available in Regular and Angle styles.
description: Giant's comes in two styles – Regular, which is bold and rugged, and Angle, which offers a cleaner, more refined take on the same hexagonal geometry. With 158 glyphs covering the essentials, it is pitched at poster and headline work where a distinctive silhouette matters more than typographic depth. A single-concept novelty face with limited range beyond display use.
foundry_blurb: Giant's Typeface takes its geometry from the basalt columns of Ireland's Giant's Causeway. The Regular style leans bold and rough; the Angle style offers a smoother interpretation of the same hexagonal forms. Strong shapes and a playful character make it suited to posters, titles and any project that wants something visually distinctive.

name: Ruma
classification_notes: Heavy geometric display face with uniform stroke weight and bold glyph forms. Available in two decorative variants: Solid (plain fill) and Hatch (striped fill). No italic, condensed, or mono cuts. Intended purely for large-scale display and headline use.
summary: A heavy geometric display face in two variants – plain Solid and striped Hatch – designed for poster, packaging and branding contexts where type needs to read as a graphic element.
description: Ruma is a bold geometric display typeface from The Native Saint Club, designed by Bagas Ferdiansah and Septianto Nugroho. It comes in two variants: Solid and Hatch, the latter applying a striped fill for a more textural, graphic treatment. With 509 glyphs including diacritics and multiple numeral sets, it is aimed squarely at headline and poster work where visual weight matters more than versatility.
foundry_blurb: A bold display typeface built around strong geometric shapes and heavy glyph forms. Comes in Solid and Hatch (striped) variants, each suited to posters, branding, packaging and street-style visuals where type needs prominence against bold imagery and saturated colour.

name: Mend Slab Typeface
classification_notes: Uppercase-only display slab serif with three corner-softness variants (Slab, Soft, Very Soft); single weight; bold and high-impact in character; no lowercase, no italic, no condensed cuts.
summary: A bold, uppercase-only display slab serif in three corner-softness variants – Slab, Soft and Very Soft – suited to branding, posters and logotypes.
description: Mend Slab is a high-impact display slab serif covering uppercase A–Z, numerals and basic punctuation across 358 glyphs. Three stylistic variants offer progressively rounded corners and serifs, allowing the tone to shift from sharp and structured to softer and more approachable. With no lowercase, italic or condensed cuts, its application is limited to headlines and display settings.
foundry_blurb: A bold, high-impact slab serif built to command attention through strong structure and expressive weight. Three variants – standard angular serifs, moderately rounded corners and progressively softened curves – let designers adjust the mood from rigid to warm. Intended for modern branding, editorial layouts, posters and logotypes.

name: N21 Typeface
classification_notes: Strictly uppercase modular display face built on a nine-square grid bisected by horizontal and vertical axes. The two styles (Regular, Retro) are design variants rather than weight steps. Very limited glyph set of 36 characters per style (uppercase, numerals, basic punctuation); no lowercase.
summary: A strictly uppercase geometric display face built on a nine-square modular grid, offered in Regular and Retro variants.
description: N21 derives every glyph from a grid of nine equal squares bisected by a central horizontal and vertical axis, with letterforms plotted from the intersection points of those guides. The outcome is a tightly controlled, architectural feel that suits editorial headlines, logotypes and experimental layouts. With only 36 glyphs per style and no lowercase, it is a narrow-use novelty rather than a general-purpose face.
foundry_blurb: An experimental display typeface inspired by Jannis Maroscheck's Shape Grammars concept. Each character is constructed from a grid of nine equal squares intersected by vertical and horizontal axes, with 130 glyphs across two styles – Regular and Retro. Intended for editorial layouts, logos and typographic projects.

name: Amantide
classification_notes: Single-weight geometric display face built from one abstract shape repeated across all glyphs. Uppercase letters and numerals only – 36 glyphs total. No lowercase, italic, condensed or mono variants. Aggressively styled, clearly intended for large-scale headline use.
summary: A single-weight geometric display face with uppercase letters and numerals only, built from one abstract form for bold, aggressive headlines.
description: Amantide was created by Alex Ortiga as title typography for his music album, which shows in its singular, uncompromising aesthetic. Every glyph derives from one abstract geometric shape, producing a bold visual rhythm suited to large-scale display work. With only 36 glyphs – uppercase letters and numbers – it is strictly a headline tool with no lowercase, no italic and no text-setting utility.
foundry_blurb: A contemporary display typeface blending sharp geometric forms with dynamic, aggressive curves. Originally designed as album title typography, Amantide builds each glyph from a single abstract shape, giving the face a bold and cohesive personality across its uppercase-only character set.

name: Obscura TM
classification_notes: Single-weight display face built around a deliberate blur and distortion aesthetic. Three stylistic sets cycle automatically via Contextual Alternates, producing unpredictable letterform variation with each keystroke. Legibility is intentionally secondary to atmosphere.
summary: A single-weight distortion display face whose three contextual alternates shuffle automatically during typing to produce deliberate visual chaos, aimed squarely at posters and nightlife graphics.
description: Obscura TM is a blurred, distortion-heavy display typeface built for the nightlife and poster circuit. Its headline feature is three stylistic sets that cycle automatically when Contextual Alternates are enabled, making each line of text visually unpredictable. At 595 glyphs – covering diacritics, ligatures, symbols and currency – it is technically complete, though the point is atmosphere rather than legibility.
foundry_blurb: Obscura TM is described as a blurry font with three stylistic sets that shuffle automatically via Contextual Alternates, giving text a unique, chaotic appearance each time it is set. The 595-glyph character set covers most popular Latin-based languages and includes diacritics, ligatures, alternates, numbers, punctuation, symbols, currency and mathematical characters. Recommended for flyers, posters and nightlife design.

name: Picnic
classification_notes: Slanted display face with soft, rounded letterforms and consistent oblique axis. Uppercase-only character set covering basic Latin, numerals and punctuation – no lowercase. Motion Blur style is a stylistic variant rather than a true optical or width variant.
summary: A slanted, uppercase-only display face with soft rounded forms and a Motion Blur style variant, aimed at logo and packaging work that wants visible personality.
description: Picnic is a display typeface built around a consistent oblique slant and rounded, soft letterforms intended to project warmth and approachability. It ships in two styles – Regular and Motion Blur – over a character set limited to uppercase letters, numerals and basic punctuation. That restricted coverage makes it a headline and logo tool rather than a general-purpose face.
foundry_blurb: Picnic brings instant personality to any design through its lively slanted letterforms and soft curves. Available in Regular and Motion Blur styles via OTF (and web formats on the extended licence), it is aimed at logos, packaging and bold branding that wants a joyful, modern aesthetic.

name: Moab Display
classification_notes: Uppercase-only bold display sans-serif with two style variants that alter counters and shoulders. No lowercase, no italic, no condensed. Y2K-inflected boxy/bubble aesthetic. Two styles are separate font files rather than weight variations.
summary: A chunky, uppercase-only display face in two style variants, built for logos and branding with a Y2K-inflected boxy character.
description: Moab Display is a bold, boxy sans-serif built for high-impact graphic work. It ships in two style variants that alter the counters and shoulders of letters, covering 218 glyphs across uppercase characters, numerals and basic punctuation. There is no lowercase, and versatility is not the point – this is a personality-led face for identity work and editorial display use.
foundry_blurb: A high-impact typeface designed to bring personality and confidence to creative work. Features generous proportions and dynamic forms across two distinct styles that transform the counters and shoulders of characters. Includes 218 unique glyphs covering uppercase letters, numerals and basic punctuation, available in OTF, WOFF and WOFF2 formats.

name: 403 Masonec
classification_notes: Modular geometric sans-serif with a brutalist character; grid-based vertical construction and circular counterforms give it a near-monospaced rhythm. The Slant variant is a mechanical oblique, not a true italic. Draws explicitly from industrial signage and brutalist architecture.
summary: A modular brutalist display sans from 403TF, built on strict grid geometry and circular counterforms for high-impact headlines and editorial work.
description: 403 Masonec is a geometric display sans-serif with an industrial character drawn from brutalist architecture and transit signage. Its grid-locked construction and circular counterforms give letterforms a near-monospaced rhythm that reads with force at large sizes. Two styles – Regular and Slant – cover 270+ Latin-based languages across a 542-glyph set that includes diacritics, ligatures, alternates and symbols.
foundry_blurb: 403TF describe Masonec as built for impact: a modular display typeface with circular counterforms and rigorous geometry suited to editorial, transit graphics, music packaging, protest graphics, poster work and motion.
designer: Umar Al Farouq, Jodi El Ghazi, Febri Riansah

name: Dirtbag TM
classification_notes: Rough hand-drawn display face with deliberate imperfections. Uses OpenType contextual alternates to cycle through three stylistic sets in a 1-2-3 rotation, simulating natural handwriting variation. Single weight; all variation comes from alternate glyphs rather than stroke contrast or weight axes.
summary: A single-weight hand-drawn display face from Type Mania, sketched and left deliberately rough, with contextual alternates rotating through three stylistic sets to keep the texture from looking mechanical.
description: Dirtbag TM is a hand-lettered display typeface built around intentional imperfection. Three stylistic sets cycle automatically via contextual alternates in a 1-2-3 pattern, avoiding the repetitive look that plagues most hand-drawn fonts. With 300 glyphs covering extended Latin scripts, it suits headlines, posters and branding where raw texture is the selling point.
foundry_blurb: A handmade display face sketched by hand and kept imperfect on purpose. Contextual alternates rotate through three stylistic sets to create organic visual texture across both print and digital use.

name: Disarm TM
classification_notes: Distressed fraktur with deliberately irregular rhythm and rough, broken details. Single weight. Stylistic Set 2 provides alternate capital letterforms. 138 glyphs total. Sits firmly in the display/novelty blackletter camp with no text-weight utility.
summary: A single-weight distressed fraktur with irregular rhythm and alternate capitals, built for gothic and grunge-leaning display work.
description: Disarm TM is a blackletter typeface from Type Mania that takes traditional fraktur structure and introduces deliberate roughness – broken strokes, uneven rhythm and worn edges that read as handmade rather than historical. A Stylistic Set 2 provides alternate capital letterforms for additional variation. Language coverage is restricted to Basic Latin, so its use is confined to display headlines and logotypes rather than any sustained typesetting.
foundry_blurb: Described by the designer as a fraktur with irregular rhythm and distressed details that evoke a raw medieval spirit. The font includes 138 glyphs covering lowercase, uppercase, diacritics, numerals, punctuation and currency, with alternate capitals accessible through Stylistic Set 2. Supplied in OTF, TTF and WOFF2 formats.

name: 403 Doshi
classification_notes: Bold geometric sans-serif built for display use; single weight available in four style variants (Regular, Slant, Soft, Soft Slant). The Slant variants are obliques rather than true italics. Soft variants substitute rounded terminals for the standard geometric finish.
designer: Umar Al Farouq, Jodi El Ghazi, Febri Riansah
summary: A bold geometric display sans by 403TF, offered in four style variants – Regular, Slant, Soft and Soft Slant – with 275 languages covered across all cuts.
description: 403 Doshi is a single-weight geometric sans built for visual impact in editorial, branding and advertising contexts. Its four styles pair the standard geometric build with a softened rounded variant, each also available as an oblique – giving designers a compact but flexible family. Language coverage is broad for an indie release, with 275 languages and 412 glyphs per style.
foundry_blurb: 403TF pitches Doshi as a bold, adaptable typeface that balances smooth curves against geometric precision, suited to digital and print work ranging from contemporary to approachable. Four style variants are included as OTF and TTF under a commercial licence.

name: Meat Display
classification_notes: Bold organic hand-drawn letterforms with rough, gritty edges and a grunge aesthetic. Two stylistic variants included, described in the listing as "two raw styles" — individual variant names are not confirmed. 101 glyphs covering uppercase, lowercase, numerals and basic punctuation. No formal weight axis. Strictly a display face; unsuitable for body text or extended setting.
summary: A chunky, hand-drawn grunge display face by Perth designer hvnter, with two raw stylistic variants built for posters, album covers and streetwear branding.
description: Meat Display packs 101 glyphs of deliberately rough, tactile letterforms into two unnamed stylistic variants that share the same gritty hand-drawn character. The range is narrow – this is strictly a headline face suited to album covers, event posters and streetwear graphics where an unpolished, energetic quality is the point. Language coverage extends to basic Latin only.
foundry_blurb: Packed with hand-drawn character, Meat Display offers two raw styles with a strong, tactile presence and plenty of flexibility for designers after gritty, energetic display type with a genuine streetwear edge.

name: Ambient TM
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif designed for display use. Its defining feature is OpenType automatic alternation between two stylistic sets that cycle circular and square letterform variants as you type, creating apparent motion within a hard-edged grid structure. Single weight only, no text-setting application.
summary: A single-weight geometric display face that auto-cycles between two stylistic sets as you type, swapping circular and square letterform variants to create the impression of movement.
description: Ambient TM is built on a hard-edged geometric grid, with all the rigidity that implies – but its gimmick is OpenType automatic alternation between two stylistic sets that shuffle circles and squares into new configurations with each keystroke. The effect is more novelty than nuance: fine for a headline or short-burst display use, but the single weight and experimental premise limit it to decorative work. It covers 254 glyphs across Basic Latin, Western European, Central European and Pan African Latin ranges.
foundry_blurb: Ambient TM takes rigid, hard-edge geometry and gives it motion. Two stylistic sets are programmed to rotate automatically as you type, shifting circles and squares into new alignments on the fly. It ships in OTF, TTF and WOFF2 formats, with commercial and extended licensing available.

name: Oldenorth
classification_notes: Single-weight decorative display face. Low cap height and flat glyph surfaces are the defining structural traits. Rounded forms paired with sharp, pointed stroke endings give it a gothic-adjacent mood without committing to blackletter construction.
summary: A single-weight decorative display face from Utrecht, defined by its unusually low cap height, flat glyph surfaces and the tension between rounded forms and sharp, pointed stroke endings.
description: Oldenorth pairs rounded letterforms with angular, pointed strokes, a combination that sits somewhere between geometric and gothic without fully committing to either. Its low cap height and idiosyncratic glyphs, notably the m and k, mark it firmly as a display face. At 309 glyphs with Latin European coverage, the character set is respectable for a novelty single-weight release.
foundry_blurb: Named after Oudenoord, a street in Utrecht where designer Peter Roeleveld developed it. The face is built around a low cap height, flat glyph surfaces and a deliberate tension between rounded shapes and sharp, pointed endings, described by the designer as simultaneously dangerous and elegant. Available as OTF on a commercial licence, with WOFF2 included on an extended licence.

name: Saku
classification_notes: Warm display serif with softened forms, originally designed for gravestone lettering. Single weight, no italic or condensed. Four stylistic sets and ligatures included. Latin European glyph coverage with diacritics.
summary: A single-weight warm serif by Peter Roeleveld, designed for gravestone lettering and carrying its softened forms well into decorative display use.
description: Saku was conceived for memorial stonecutting, with soft serifs intended to bring warmth to names carved in cold stone. The design translates to decorative display contexts, backed by 430 glyphs, ligatures and four stylistic sets. It ships as a single Roman cut with no italic, condensed or mono companion.
foundry_blurb: Saku was initially designed for use on gravestones, with soft serifs giving names a warm and friendly quality against cold stone materials. The typeface suits decorative applications through its combination of capitals and lowercase letters, offering a Latin European character set with diacritics, ligatures and four stylistic sets.

name: Latrodectus Hasselti
classification_notes: Single-weight experimental display face with a fixed 10° slant baked into the design and pronounced thick-to-thin stroke contrast. No separate italic or oblique variant – the slant is structural. Named after the redback spider species Latrodectus hasseltii. 365 glyphs, 64 ligatures, Latin European diacritic coverage.
summary: A single-weight experimental display face by Paloma Plana, built on a fixed 10° slant and sharp thick-to-thin contrast, with 365 glyphs and 64 ligatures covering Latin European scripts.
description: Latrodectus Hasselti is a display typeface designed by Paloma Plana in 2020, named after the redback spider. The design is defined by a 10° structural slant and high stroke contrast, lending it a sharp, graphic quality suited to experimental editorial headlines and poster work. It ships as a single weight with 365 glyphs, 64 ligatures and full Latin European diacritic support.
foundry_blurb: An unconventional display typeface with strong contrasts between thick and thin strokes and a distinctive built-in 10° slant. Ships with 365 glyphs – including 64 ligatures, diacritics, numbers, punctuation, currency and mathematical characters – across the Latin European alphabet. Available under commercial or extended licence in OTF and TTF; WOFF and WOFF2 included with the extended licence.

name: Bootzy Condensed TM
classification_notes: Single-weight condensed display sans-serif with a rough, DIY-print aesthetic. Three stylistic sets provide automatic glyph alternation. 426 glyphs including diacritics, ligatures, alternates, numbers, punctuation and currency symbols. Not a multi-weight family.
summary: A single-weight condensed display sans-serif with a rough, bootleg-print aesthetic built for zines, flyers and underground creative work.
description: Bootzy Condensed TM is a condensed display sans-serif from Type Mania that leans into DIY culture with deliberately raw, printed letterforms. Three stylistic sets with automatic glyph alternation keep the handmade feel across longer settings. At 426 glyphs – including diacritics, ligatures and currency symbols – it covers most Latin-based languages.
foundry_blurb: A rugged display sans-serif born from the creative underground, drawing on the DIY ethos of bootlegging. Designed for flyers, zines and rebellious creative applications, with three stylistic sets, diacritics and broad Latin language support. Available in OTF, TTF and WOFF2.

name: Hiker TM
classification_notes: Informal handwritten script with intentionally rough, imperfect letterforms. Two OpenType stylistic sets enable automatic alternation between glyph variants, lending a more organic, hand-drawn character. 382 glyphs total, including diacritics, ligatures, alternates, currency and mathematical symbols.
summary: A single-weight handwritten script from Type Mania with a raw, lo-fi underground edge, suited to flyers, posters and branding that matches the aesthetic.
description: Hiker TM leans into rough, imperfect letterforms for a street-adjacent, smoked-out look. Two OpenType stylistic sets cycle between glyph alternates automatically, lending a more convincingly hand-drawn quality to set text. At its best on posters and flyers where the brief calls for something edgy rather than polished.
foundry_blurb: Type Mania positions Hiker TM as the go-to for unique and unconventional handwriting vibes, sitting at the underground end of the spectrum with a lo-fi, smoked-out aesthetic suited to flyers, posters, branding and campaigns.

name: Bleep 01 TM
classification_notes: Listed as sans-serif on Creative Market but functions exclusively as a display face — single weight, strong retro-futuristic character, 80s/Y2K visual associations, no text-setting utility. Classified as display here to reflect actual use case.
summary: A single-weight experimental display face from Type Mania, drawing on 80s digital nostalgia and Y2K aesthetics for headline and identity work.
description: Bleep 01 TM blends retro digital feel with contemporary graphic sensibility, aimed at designers who want a distinctive headline voice. It ships in one weight with around 192 glyphs covering Latin-based languages. The italic companion lives in a separate release, Bleep 02 TM.
