foundry_blurb: Bleep 01 TM pairs modern aesthetics with cozy retro feels, made for designers, developers and digital artists looking for a distinctive visual identity. Suited to logos, posters, branding, headings and digital projects.

name: Device TM
classification_notes: Uppercase-only display typeface with a deliberately eccentric, high-contrast character. Single weight. No italic or condensed. 197 glyphs covering Latin-based languages with diacritics, ligatures, punctuation and currency signs.
summary: An uppercase-only display face with a deliberately edgy, offbeat personality, suited to short-burst graphic work like posters and t-shirt graphics.
description: Device TM is a single-weight, all-caps display typeface with an unconventional, bold character designed for high-impact print applications. It covers 197 glyphs, including diacritics, ligatures, currency signs and punctuation, giving it functional reach across popular Latin-based languages. Its utility is limited by the absence of lowercase and any additional weights or styles.
foundry_blurb: 6TM's shop pitches Device TM as unapologetically bold and fiercely quirky, with an edgy demeanour aimed at flyers, posters and t-shirt graphics. Available under commercial and extended licences in OTF, TTF and WOFF2 formats.

name: Cube TM
classification_notes: A display-weight geometric sans-serif with heavy brutalist influence. Blunt, rigid stroke terminals. The defining feature is three OpenType stylistic sets that cycle automatically during typesetting, breaking visual monotony without manual intervention. Single weight; no italics or condensed cuts.
summary: A single-weight brutalist display face that uses three auto-alternating stylistic sets to introduce rhythm and variation into otherwise rigid, blunt geometry.
description: Cube TM takes the blunt stroke terminals and rigid structure of brutalist design, then undercuts the monotony with an OpenType trick: three stylistic sets rotate automatically as text is set, so consecutive glyphs shift form without manual selection. The effect is somewhere between severe and playful. At 314 glyphs with diacritic and currency support, the coverage is solid for a single-weight display release, though it is built for headlines and posters rather than running copy.
foundry_blurb: Described by the designer as a brutalist font with a twist, Cube TM blends rigid forms with unexpected rhythm. Three built-in stylistic sets alternate automatically, varying letterforms across a line of text without any manual intervention. The font ships in OTF, TTF and WOFF2 formats, includes 314 glyphs, and supports the most widely used Latin-based languages.

name: Garly Typeface
classification_notes: Bold rounded sans-serif display face, evolved from Grand Mottley Sans by the same studio. Bold weight only, available in Regular and Slanted (oblique) variants. Retro-inflected, playful letterforms with broad diacritic coverage across 501 glyphs.
summary: A rounded bold display sans from Indonesia's The Native Saint Club, built on the bones of Grand Mottley Sans with softer edges and 501 glyphs across two styles.
description: Garly is a bold rounded display typeface from The Native Saint Club, a studio based in Klaten, Indonesia. It arrives in Regular and Slanted styles with 501 glyphs – covering diacritical marks, ligatures and three numeral sets. Its friendly, warm character suits posters, branding and contemporary display work where personality is needed without aggression.
foundry_blurb: A bold display typeface with rounded, playful letterforms built for projects that need warmth and presence. An evolved take on Grand Mottley Sans with softer edges and refined character shapes – approachable and adaptable across a wide range of design contexts.

name: Bleep 02 TM
classification_notes: Listed as sans-serif on third-party platforms, but the retro-futurist aesthetic and headline-only scope make display the more accurate categorisation. Single-weight italic only — the upright counterpart is sold separately as Bleep 01 TM. Both are treated as distinct products rather than a unified family.
summary: An experimental single-weight italic display sans with retro-futurist character, released in 2024 as the italic companion to Bleep 01 TM.
description: Bleep 02 TM is a single-weight italic display typeface from Type Mania, released in July 2024. It pairs with the upright Bleep 01 TM, sharing what the designer describes as a blend of modern aesthetics and cozy retro sensibility. With 191 glyphs covering Latin-based scripts, it is aimed at logotypes, headings and branded digital content rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: Bleep 02 TM brings experimental cozy vibes to the Bleep series as its italic companion, mixing modern aesthetics with a retro sensibility suited to distinctive visual identities. Targeted at designers and digital artists, the font ships in OTF, TTF and WOFF2 formats under commercial and extended licence tiers.

name: Lovely Mess Handwritten Chaotic Sans
classification_notes: All-caps hand-drawn sans serif with deliberately imperfect, organic letterforms. Marketed as a chaotic/expressive display face. Single weight only. Despite listing both "uppercase" and "lowercase" in features, it is an all-caps design throughout.
summary: A hand-drawn all-caps display sans by Victoria Strukovskaya, built on deliberately rough, organic letterforms aimed at trend-driven posters and bold branding.
description: Lovely Mess is a single-weight all-caps sans with 199 glyphs, covering Latin European languages alongside numerals, punctuation and currency symbols. The letterforms are intentionally imperfect, carrying the energy of casual handwriting without the formal rhythm of a proper script. Best suited to Gen Z-facing work: expressive posters, playful logos and packaging where an unpolished, chaotic feel is the point.
foundry_blurb: A relaxed, all-caps hand-drawn sans with quirky edges and an unpolished personality. Available in OTF and TTF formats (WOFF and WOFF2 on the extended licence) with a 199-glyph Latin European character set.

name: Brivela Display
classification_notes: Hand-sketched, chunky display face with graffiti and urban street lettering influence. Single weight only. No italic or condensed variants. Thick, irregular strokes with deliberate rawness throughout the character set.
summary: A chunky, hand-sketched graffiti display face from Indonesian designer Ahmad Nur Alfian, built for loud street-aesthetic applications like posters, album covers and apparel.
description: Brivela Display draws on urban graffiti lettering, with thick, irregular hand-drawn strokes in a single bold weight, released under the Uncarving Nation label in September 2025. The 430-plus glyph set covers Latin European languages, six numeral sets and includes ligatures. Its appeal is limited to contexts where raw, city-aesthetic type is the explicit point.
foundry_blurb: A bold urban display font with street lettering energy, designed for high-impact work including posters, album artwork, apparel and logos. Ships in OTF, TTF and web formats with 430-plus glyphs and Latin European language coverage.

name: Duster TM
classification_notes: Single-weight heavy distressed display typeface built on sans-serif letterforms overlaid with a heavy weathered texture. Three OpenType stylistic sets enable automatic glyph alternation to reduce visual repetition when the same character appears in sequence. Unsuitable for body text; pitched squarely at headline and poster use.
summary: A heavy distressed display face with sans-serif bones and three stylistic sets for automatic glyph alternation, built for underground event graphics and bold headline work.
description: Duster TM is a single-weight display typeface built on heavy sans-serif letterforms with a worn, gritty surface texture. It covers 367 glyphs across uppercase and lowercase, including diacritics, ligatures and alternates for Latin-based languages. Three stylistic sets shift glyphs automatically when the same letter appears in sequence, preventing the mechanical repetition common in distressed display faces.
foundry_blurb: Duster TM adds a weathered, worn-in look to any bold layout. Suited to underground event flyers, social media campaigns and dynamic poster work, it ships with 367 glyphs including diacritics, ligatures, alternates, currency and punctuation, plus three stylistic sets that automatically vary glyphs when placed side by side.

name: Eparpille
classification_notes: Dot-based experimental display type. Letters form through fragmentation and reformation of swarm-like dots. Three stylistic variants – Sharp, Medium, Cloud – represent degrees of dot density or cohesion rather than traditional weight steps. No italic or condensed cuts.
summary: An experimental dot-based display face in three stylistic cuts – Sharp, Medium and Cloud – where letters form through the fragmentation and reformation of swarm-like dots.
description: Eparpille is built as a coded system in which letters emerge from a swarm-like motion of dots, producing three distinct styles: Sharp, Medium and Cloud. The 462-glyph set includes diacritics and basic punctuation, giving it workable Latin coverage. It is aimed squarely at bold editorial layouts, visual experiments and digital art rather than extended reading.
foundry_blurb: Described by its designer as built as a coded system, Eparpille explores fragmentation and reformation through a swarm-like motion of dots. Three static styles are offered – Sharp, Medium and Cloud – though the designer also produced a variable animation as a separate visual experiment not included in the download. The release targets bold editorial layouts, visual experiments and digital art projects.

name: Ornamentum
classification_notes: Modular geometric display face built on a strict grid; each character doubles as a decorative building block for pattern work. Uppercase-only, 41 glyphs in total – no lowercase, no italic, no condensed.
summary: A grid-based modular display face by Hugo Jourdan where each uppercase letter doubles as a building block for ornamental pattern work.
description: Ornamentum sits in the geometric ornamental tradition, each character drawn on a strict grid so letters can tile into repeating decorative patterns. The release covers uppercase only – three weights, 41 glyphs in total, with numbers and basic punctuation included. Suited to logotypes, display headlines and pattern-based layouts; it is not viable for running text.
foundry_blurb: Ornamentum is a modular display typeface blending geometric and ornamental style; characters are designed on a strict grid to work as standalone letters and as interlocking components for building intricate patterns, making it suited to experimental typography, visual identities and decorative layouts.

name: Offset TM
classification_notes: Single-weight distressed display typeface with sans-serif underlying structure. Three OpenType stylistic sets auto-shuffle through glyph alternates. 589 glyphs including diacritics, ligatures and alternates. Grunge/punk sensibility; not suited to body text.
summary: A single-weight distressed display face from Type Mania with three auto-shuffling stylistic sets that push glyph alternates automatically, giving type a roughened, organic rhythm.
description: Offset TM is a rugged sans-serif-derived display typeface released in 2024 by Type Mania, built around OpenType stylistic sets that cycle through alternates as you type, producing text with natural variation and a grunge-inflected texture. The 589-glyph set covers uppercase, lowercase, diacritics, ligatures and alternates across Latin-based languages. It suits poster headlines, packaging and identity work where distressed character is deliberate.
foundry_blurb: A dynamic display typeface combining rugged aesthetics with three stylistic sets that shuffle through glyph alternates automatically, adding character without manual intervention. Supplied as OTF, TTF and WOFF2 with support for the most popular Latin-based languages.

name: Lucid Drift Pixel Surreal Script
classification_notes: A script typeface with a pixel/digital aesthetic. Rounded dot terminals and smooth stroke transitions create a hybrid between structured digital letterforms and flowing handwritten script. Unusual combination that doesn't slot cleanly into pure script or pure display pixel categories.
summary: A single-weight pixel script that combines structured digital dot terminals with a loose handwritten rhythm, aimed at expressive branding and editorial work.
description: Lucid Drift Pixel Surreal Script blends pixel-art construction with the flowing quality of handwritten lettering. Rounded dot terminals and smooth transitions give it a drifting, calm feel that sits somewhere between retro digital aesthetics and contemporary script. With 114 glyphs covering Latin European characters, it is pitched at posters, branding and editorial contexts where a touch of the surreal is welcome.
foundry_blurb: Described by the shop as a surreal pixel script balancing structured digital forms with a soft, flowing handwritten rhythm. Sold with commercial and extended licence options in OTF, TTF and web formats.

name: Gloopie
classification_notes: Abstract handwritten display script; single regular weight; smooth, bouncy letterforms with a Y2K aesthetic; includes stylistic ligatures for oo, tt and ff, plus alternate glyphs for c, e and s.
summary: A single-weight abstract handwritten script with smooth, bouncy curves, Y2K charm and a handful of stylistic ligatures and alternate glyphs.
description: Gloopie is a display script by Victoria Strukovskaya built around a fluid, bouncy rhythm suited to logos, posters and apparel graphics. Its 203-glyph Latin European set includes ligatures for oo, tt and ff alongside alternate forms for c, e and s. It is a one-weight novelty face, best reserved for informal display contexts at larger sizes.
foundry_blurb: Billed as a playful, fluid handwritten font with smooth curves and quirky ligatures, Gloopie is aimed at eye-catching logos, vibrant posters, stylish branding and trendy apparel. It ships with 203 glyphs covering most popular Latin-based languages, available as OTF and TTF under a commercial licence, with WOFF and WOFF2 added on an extended licence.

name: Zine TM
classification_notes: Typewriter-inspired design in a single Regular weight. The typewriter aesthetic implies monospaced or near-monospaced spacing; marketed as a creative/display face rather than a utility mono. 197 glyphs with ligatures, diacritics, currency and maths symbols. No italic or condensed variants.
summary: A retro typewriter-styled face from Type Mania, available in a single weight with ligature and diacritic support for Latin-based languages.
description: Zine TM takes its cues from typewriter typography, offering a nostalgic texture dressed up with a contemporary edge. It ships in one Regular weight with 197 glyphs, covering broad Latin diacritics, ligatures, currency symbols and basic maths operators. Available as OTF and TTF under commercial licence, with WOFF2 added on the extended tier.
foundry_blurb: A typewriter-inspired font that steps back in time while celebrating contemporary design sensibilities. Includes ligatures, diacritical support for popular Latin-based languages, and currency and mathematical symbols, sold under commercial and extended licence options.

name: The Bold Era
classification_notes: Single-weight chunky display sans with wide letterforms, ultra-tight tracking and soft curves. Retro-inflected with a bubbly, playful character. 199 glyphs covering Latin European characters including diacritics, numbers, punctuation, symbols and currency.
summary: A single-weight chunky display sans with ultra-tight spacing and soft retro curves, designed for loud poster and headline work.
description: The Bold Era is a wide, compact display sans with soft curves and ultra-tight tracking that gives it a confident, slightly playful feel. The retro-inflected letterforms suit posters, merchandise and album covers where bold impact matters more than text setting. One weight only limits its range, but within that narrow brief it is competently executed.
foundry_blurb: Blends retro nostalgia with a modern bubbly attitude. Wide, confident letterforms with ultra-tight spacing make words feel loud, stylish and a little playful. Best suited to posters, branding, merch, album covers and bold headlines, particularly when paired with vibrant colours and vintage-inspired layouts.

name: Dopamine Script Playful Vibe Font
classification_notes: Casual hand-drawn script with loose, organic strokes and deliberate imperfections. Single weight. 197 glyphs including diacritics for Latin European languages.
summary: A single-weight hand-drawn script by Victoria Strukovskaya with loose, organic strokes aimed at branding, apparel and packaging projects.
description: Dopamine Script is a casual hand-drawn typeface with deliberately rough, spontaneous strokes and organic imperfections. It covers 197 glyphs in a single weight, including diacritics for most Latin European languages. Its relaxed character suits contemporary branding and packaging where an unpolished, personal aesthetic is the goal.
foundry_blurb: A relaxed, confident hand-drawn typeface built to bring natural rhythm and character to design work, balancing spontaneity with enough clarity for branding, apparel, packaging and editorial applications. Available under commercial and extended licences in OTF, TTF and web font formats.

name: Radial Typeface
classification_notes: Experimental display face where every letterform is plotted within a strict radial grid. Characters are not drawn freely but derived from the geometric possibilities of the grid system itself. Inspired by Buckminster Fuller's spatial and systems thinking. Single cut, Wide, with 111 glyphs covering Latin uppercase and lowercase, numerals, punctuation and basic symbols.
summary: A single-weight geometric display face where each character is derived from the spatial logic of a strict radial grid, developed from Liad Shadmi's Alphabetical Room project.
description: Radial plots every letterform within a fixed radial grid, constraining each character to the geometric possibilities that structure allows. The typeface grew from Shadmi's Alphabetical Room research project and draws on Buckminster Fuller's systems thinking. It ships as one Wide cut with 111 glyphs – practical only for headline or display work where the grid concept is central to the intent.
foundry_blurb: A geometric typeface built on a strict radial grid structure, each character shaped by the possibilities that system allows. Developed from the experimental project The Alphabetical Room and informed by architect and systems theorist Richard Buckminster Fuller. Available in OTF and TTF for commercial use, with WOFF and WOFF2 formats included in the extended licence.

name: EVO2
classification_notes: Six-style display type by Alex Ortiga. Three weight tiers — Regular, Massive, Extreme — each paired with an oblique cut. No true italic; obliques only. 108 glyphs covering the Latin alphabet with basic numerals, punctuation, symbols and currency. Escalating distortion from clean geometric forms at Regular to overtly deconstructed shapes at Extreme. Optimised for large-scale graphic use rather than text setting.
summary: A six-style futuristic display type that steps from clean Regular through distorted Extreme, each weight paired with an oblique cut, built for poster work and bold graphic branding.
description: EVO2 is the follow-up to Alex Ortiga's EVO, expanding the family to six styles across three weight tiers — Regular, Massive and Extreme — each available in upright and oblique cuts. The design plays structural precision against deliberate distortion, with Extreme variants pushing glyphs into overtly experimental territory. At 108 glyphs it covers Latin basics only, positioning it squarely as a tool for visual impact: posters, music artwork and experimental branding.
foundry_blurb: A bold, futuristic display typeface built for maximum visual impact. EVO2 balances structure and chaos across six stylistic variants, ranging from clean precision to extreme distortion, with intended use in posters, logos and bold branding projects.

name: Badger Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight hand-drawn display face built on raw marker strokes and street-style lettering. Irregular organic letterforms with sharp turns and spontaneous construction. Limited glyph set of 63 characters covering basic Latin.
summary: A single-weight hand-drawn display face from designer hvnter, built on raw marker strokes and street-style lettering for high-energy posters, streetwear and zine work.
description: Badger draws its character from spontaneous marker strokes and irregular letterforms, with sharp turns and organic shapes that project movement and attitude. The single-weight release covers 63 glyphs – uppercase, lowercase, numerals and basic symbols – keeping scope deliberately narrow. It suits high-impact applications where a rough, hand-crafted aesthetic matters more than typographic range.
foundry_blurb: An energetic typeface inspired by street-style lettering and marker work, with irregular shapes, sharp turns and spontaneous flow. Aimed at posters, album artwork, streetwear branding, zines and social media visuals. Available with a commercial OTF licence or an extended licence covering OTF, WOFF and WOFF2 formats.

name: Candy Display
classification_notes: Uppercase-only display typeface with generous, rounded letterforms and a strong pop aesthetic. Three styles — Regular, Italic, and Backwards — with no additional weights. 197 glyphs total. Created in Adobe Illustrator and Fontself by Adhemas Batista and published in early 2026.
summary: A bold, uppercase-only display face with rounded, pop-inflected letterforms — best suited to headline work and expressive branding rather than any setting requiring mixed case or extended text.
description: Candy Display is a chunky, cheerful display typeface by Adhemas Batista built around generous curves and a pop-art energy. It comes in three styles — Regular, Italic, and a Backwards variant that flips the letterforms for unconventional compositions. The character set is uppercase only, which keeps the use cases narrow, though within its range it delivers consistent rhythm and personality.
foundry_blurb: A vibrant display font designed for impact and personality. Its three styles — Regular, Italic, and Backwards — offer creative flexibility for pop-inspired branding, eye-catching titles, and expressive visual identities. Available as OTF under commercial licence, with WOFF and WOFF2 included in the extended licence.

name: Mamoth
classification_notes: Single-weight rounded display sans-serif with soft, bubbly curves. Bold in character rather than weight range; designed purely for display and identity work. No italic, condensed or mono cuts. Closer to a novelty display face than a workhorse sans-serif.
summary: A single-weight rounded display face with soft, bubbly curves suited to logos and packaging where a warm, approachable tone is wanted.
description: Mamoth is a bold, rounded sans-serif from indie designer hvnter, built for brand and logo work rather than body text. Its soft curves and cheerful personality suit packaging, custom lettering and identity projects that need warmth without rigidity. One weight and basic Latin coverage keep it firmly in single-use territory.
foundry_blurb: A bold, bubbly rounded typeface designed to add charm and personality to designs. Soft curves and a cheerful style make it well suited to logos, brand identities and packaging. Comes with 100+ glyphs including bonus illustration characters; available as OTF for commercial use and OTF, WOFF and WOFF2 under an extended licence.

name: Virage
classification_notes: Variable display typeface with a motorsport theme. Rounded forms and straight strokes evoke racetrack geometry; square counter-forms reference the checkered flag. Five named weight stops (Thin to Bold) with continuous variable interpolation. 116-glyph coverage suggests basic Latin plus diacritics only.
summary: A variable display face by Valentin Normand drawn from motorsport aesthetics, with rounded forms, straight strokes and square counter-forms across five weight stops.
description: Virage spans five weights from Thin to Bold, with variable font technology enabling continuous interpolation between them. Its rounded letterforms and straight-line contrasts reference racing circuit geometry, while square counter-forms nod to the checkered flag. At 116 glyphs it covers basic Latin characters and diacritics, keeping scope narrow and the concept consistent.
foundry_blurb: A typeface built around speed, control and endurance, with fluid weight modulation as its central idea. Rounded shapes and straight lines evoke racetrack trajectories; square counter-forms reference the checkered flag. Aimed at graphic projects centred on performance, technology or competitive themes.

name: Metallika TM
classification_notes: Single-weight metal-inflected script with OpenType automatic stylistic alternation between two sets; distressed, punk-derived letterforms; 388 glyphs covering Basic Latin, Western European, Central European and Pan African Latin ranges. Creative Market lists it explicitly as a script font; the 6TM shop describes it as a dark experimental display typeface.
summary: A single-weight grunge script from Type Mania with automatic stylistic alternation, built squarely for album covers, posters and metal-adjacent graphic work.
description: Metallika TM is a rugged, distressed script drawing on punk and heavy metal lettering traditions. It ships with 388 glyphs – diacritics, ligatures and alternates included – and uses OpenType programming to automatically swap between two stylistic sets when the same letter appears consecutively, creating irregular, handmade-feeling text. Best used as a headline or logotype element in music, zine and merchandise design where the rough aesthetic is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Marketed as a dark experimental display typeface suited to album covers, posters and merchandise. Features two stylistic sets with automatic glyph alternation for dynamic visual variation, plus full Latin extended character support including diacritics, ligatures, numerals and currency symbols.

name: Mycela
classification_notes: Organic display typeface inspired by mycelium growth patterns. Single weight with 300 glyphs, including ligatures and alternates. Latin European coverage. Letterform design prioritises character combinations over individual glyph aesthetics.
summary: A single-weight organic display face by Peter Roeleveld, drawn from the growth logic of mycelium, where the beauty of the letterforms emerges from combinations rather than any individual glyph.
description: Mycela takes its concept from fungal networks, with letterforms designed to read as connected systems rather than isolated characters. It covers 300 glyphs across Latin European diacritics, ligatures and alternates. As a single-weight display face, it suits editorial headlines and experimental short-form type work.
foundry_blurb: Named after mycelium – the vegetative part of fungi – Mycela was designed around the idea that beauty lies in character combinations rather than individual glyphs. The face includes 300 glyphs covering Latin European diacritics, ligatures and alternates, available as OTF under commercial or extended licence.

name: Foster Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight, uppercase-only display typeface with futuristic and retro-Y2K character shapes. No italic, condensed or monospace variants exist; variation comes from 100+ alternate glyphs within a single OTF file rather than a weight family. Limited character set: uppercase A-Z, numerals 0-9 and basic symbols only.
summary: A single-weight uppercase display face with a Y2K-futuristic aesthetic, built around over 100 alternate glyphs rather than a traditional weight family.
description: Foster is a customisable uppercase display typeface designed for bold headlines, custom wordmarks and poster work. Its letterforms draw on futuristic and retro-inspired shapes with cyberpunk and Y2K references, suited to album covers, branding and digital media. Customisation relies on over 100 alternate glyphs within a single OTF file rather than a weight or style family.
foundry_blurb: A highly customisable display typeface featuring over 100 alternate glyphs for creating distinctive custom type. Covers uppercase A–Z, numerals 0–9 and basic symbols, and is designed to help build unique wordmarks for posters, branding and digital projects.

name: Dummy TM
classification_notes: Heavy single-weight distressed display typeface with three OpenType stylistic sets that rotate glyph alternates automatically as you type, providing visual variety without multiple weights or styles.
summary: A heavy, single-weight distressed display face with three rotating stylistic alternates, built for street-oriented print work such as flyers, record sleeves and T-shirt graphics.
description: Dummy TM is a bold, worn-down display typeface by Type Mania that leans into street lettering and grunge aesthetics. It ships with 590 glyphs and three automatic stylistic sets that rotate letterforms as you type, giving natural variation across a composition without manual alternate selection. The coverage spans uppercase, lowercase, diacritics, ligatures, punctuation and currency symbols across most popular Latin-script languages.
foundry_blurb: Pitched as the go-to for heavy distressed type, Dummy TM uses three auto-rotating stylistic sets to keep letterforms from looking repetitive across flyers, record covers and T-shirt prints. Available in OTF and TTF under commercial and extended licences, with WOFF2 included in the extended tier.

name: Felony Condensed
classification_notes: Condensed ink-bleed display typeface with heavy grunge distressing. Single OTF weight, Latin character set only (96 glyphs). Novelty/decorative — no optical refinement or spacing finesse to speak of. Suits headline-only use.
summary: A single-weight condensed display font with ink-bleed distressing, built for gig posters and album artwork where raw edge matters more than refinement.
description: Felony Condensed is a grunge-inflected display typeface by Australian designer Will McNeill, built around heavy ink-bleed texture and tight condensed proportions. It targets headline use on posters, album covers and underground graphic work. The character set covers uppercase, lowercase, numerals and basic punctuation in a single OTF file.
foundry_blurb: An ink-bleed grunge display font suited to posters, album covers and urban design projects that need attitude. Includes uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, punctuation and symbols; available as OTF for commercial use, with WOFF and WOFF2 added on the extended licence.

name: Formung Typeface
classification_notes: Constructive modular letterforms with sharp insets and rounded transitions. Not a conventional serif or sans-serif; sits squarely in the experimental display category with a futuristic, sculptural quality.
summary: A single-weight experimental display face by Johannes Thiel, built on modular, constructive principles with sharp insets softened by rounded transitions for a futuristic, sculptural effect.
description: Formung is an experimental display typeface from German designer Johannes Thiel. Its letterforms follow constructive, modular logic – sharp geometric insets meet smoothly rounded edges, producing a visual tension that reads as futuristic and almost three-dimensional. With 110 glyphs covering Latin letters, figures, punctuation and symbols, it is strictly a headline and graphic-design tool rather than a workhorse text face.
foundry_blurb: An experimental display typeface with a strong graphic presence, built on constructive, modular principles softened by smooth transitions between sharp insets and rounded edges. The result is a futuristic, almost sculptural aesthetic suited to high-impact graphic design work.

name: Fable Dust
classification_notes: Medieval-inspired display face with eccentric hand-inked serifs, intentional stroke irregularity and grunge texturing throughout. Gothic influences are present but the font reads as a grunge display rather than a true blackletter — letters retain recognisable Latin forms beneath the texture. No weights or styles beyond the single cut.
summary: A single-weight medieval grunge display face with hand-inked eccentricity, built for dark editorial and occult-adjacent branding at large sizes.
description: Fable Dust is a whimsical, medieval-inspired display typeface from designer Softulka, drawing on ancient manuscript aesthetics and gothic letterform traditions. Irregular strokes, organic imperfections and grunge texturing give it an explicitly handcrafted feel. With 193 glyphs including diacritics, it suits book covers, album art, vintage posters and dark-toned branding, though its narrow tonal range limits it to headline work.
foundry_blurb: Fable Dust is described as a whimsical medieval display font capturing the essence of ancient manuscripts and forgotten fairytales, with eccentric serifs, hand-inked irregularities and gothic grunge texturing for a rustic, handcrafted aesthetic. Sold with commercial and extended licensing options in OTF, TTF and WOFF formats.

name: LD_AK Typeface
classification_notes: Variable display typeface defined by angular corner junctions that replace conventional curved or straight stroke joins. Characters flow rhythmically through these centre-linked corners. Compressed-to-extended bold range via variable axis. Small glyph count (110) confirms it is purpose-built for display, not text.
summary: A geometric variable display face from Lundqvist & Dallyn, built around a distinctive corner-junction construction that gives each glyph an angular, rhythmically consistent character.
description: LD_AK is defined by its corner connectors: stroke junctions meet at a point rather than aligning vertically or horizontally, then link through the glyph's centre to produce a consistent visual rhythm. The variable axis runs from compressed to extended bold, giving it useful range for headline work. At 110 glyphs it covers letters, diacritics, numerals, punctuation and arrows, with OTF, TTF and web font formats available.
foundry_blurb: LD_AK is a variable typeface distinguished by corner-connected junctions that create rhythmic flow across each character. The weight and width axes allow compression to extension across bold variants, making it adaptable for display-focused design work.

name: Legion
classification_notes: Bold oblique display face where the slant is integral to the design rather than a separate italic variant. Single style, no weight range. Extensive alternates but narrow typographic scope.
summary: A bold oblique display face with 190 glyphs and over 120 alternates, built for logo and brand lettering work.
description: Legion is a single-style bold oblique typeface designed for high-impact display use. It carries 190 glyphs with an extensive set of letter alternates intended to give logos and custom lettering a distinctive edge. Available in OTF for commercial use, with WOFF and WOFF2 added under the extended licence.
foundry_blurb: Described as a bold, slanted typeface built to give typography projects a powerful edge, Legion offers over 120 letter variations across 190 glyphs for use in logos, brand identities and custom lettering.

name: 403 Edsonna
classification_notes: Geometric-grotesque sans-serif with squared terminals and wide, upright proportions in the Technical Brutalism vein. Slant styles are geometric obliques, not true italics. Variable font technology spanning five weight axes.
designer: Umar Al Farouq, Jodi El Ghazi, Febri Riansah (403TF)
summary: A variable grotesque with squared terminals and a cinematic stance, built for brutalist layouts, dashboards and industrial brand work.
description: 403 Edsonna is a technical sans-serif designed for precision-heavy contexts: information grids, UI dashboards and editorial systems. Its squared terminals and wide, upright proportions hold well at small sizes without losing presence at display scale. Five weights with matching obliques, variable font technology and support for over 308 languages make it practical across most typographic scenarios.
foundry_blurb: The listing positions Edsonna within "Technical Brutalism", drawing its design language from terminal data streams, logistics labelling and architectural schematics. The foundry pitches it for UI/UX work, automotive and tech branding, brutalist editorial layouts and music festival collateral, with variable font technology and 692 glyphs per weight.

name: Gruwel
classification_notes: Single-weight experimental display face with sharp, angular letterforms and a raw underground-techno aesthetic. No traditional type classification applies; sits closest to post-punk or industrial display. Not a blackletter despite the dark theme — letterforms are custom and highly stylised rather than calligraphic.
summary: A single-weight experimental display face by Peter Roeleveld, built around razor-sharp fanged letterforms drawn from the designer's dark techno influences, with the Dutch name meaning "horror".
description: Gruwel is a display typeface by Dutch designer Peter Roeleveld, channelling the raw energy of underground techno through sharply angular letterforms with edges described as resembling animal fangs. The 116-glyph set covers full upper and lowercase Latin, numerals, punctuation, arrows and mathematical operators, available in a single Regular weight. It suits editorial headlines, poster work and brand applications with a deliberate underground or dark-culture aesthetic.
foundry_blurb: Gruwel represents the raw, sharp aesthetic of Peter Roeleveld's personality, crafted while listening to the grimmest and darkest techno. The letterforms carry edges reminiscent of animal fangs, and the name — Dutch for "horror" — sets the tone for what the typeface is trying to do.

name: Trolha Typeface
classification_notes: Experimental modular display typeface built from five core components; each uppercase letter ships in four distinct variations. Uppercase-only, single weight, 139 glyphs. Designed by CALA Studio.
summary: A Portuguese-inspired modular display face from CALA Studio, where every uppercase letter has four distinct variations constructed from five shared geometric components.
description: Trolha is built around a strict modular system: five core components combine to produce every character, with each letter available in four variations. The result is a playful, expressive toolkit for headlines and short-form display work. Uppercase only, single weight, 139 glyphs total.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by "Marteladas" — Portuguese for hammering pieces together — Trolha assembles every letter from five shared components, each available in four distinct forms. Sold as OTF for commercial use, with WOFF and WOFF2 formats added on the extended licence.

name: Aggram Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight display typeface with sharp terminal finishes and sleek geometric forms. Only 64 glyphs covering basic Latin – no extended character support. No weight variants, italics or condensed styles available. Designed explicitly for headline and large-scale editorial use.
summary: A slim, single-weight display font from French designer Jules Bigot, built for editorial headlines with sharp terminal finishes and clean geometric forms.
description: Aggram is a minimal display typeface from Jules Bigot (Big Concrete Planet), characterised by crisp lines and sharp finishes suited to contemporary graphic work. At 64 glyphs, it covers basic Latin only – enough for headline and logotype use, not body copy or multilingual applications. It ships in a single weight with no italic or condensed companion.
foundry_blurb: An elegant typeface with sharp finishes, designed for striking headlines, editorial projects and contemporary visual compositions. Available as an OTF file (WOFF and WOFF2 under the extended licence) containing 64 glyphs including letters, numbers and basic punctuation.

name: Razor
classification_notes: Experimental display face built on slanted, sharp-edged letterforms with angular and occasionally wavy forms. Single weight. Very limited character set of 45 glyphs (letters, numerals, basic punctuation). Geometric in construction with abstract, unconventional proportions.
summary: A sharp, angular experimental display face from Carlos Gonçalves with slanted letterforms and a tight 45-glyph set, conceived as a formal exercise in edge and angle.
description: Razor is a single-weight display typeface built around slanted characters with super-sharp edges, extreme angles and occasional wavy forms. Its 45-glyph character set makes it a formal experiment rather than a production workhorse – consistent internal logic holds the family together, but coverage is too thin for extended text. Best suited to short headlines, poster work or motion graphics where an abstract, aggressive personality is the point.
foundry_blurb: The shop listing describes Razor as an exercise and play with form – slanted characters with sharp, unusual angles and wavy details, designed around consistent base rules that keep the family coherent despite its experimental nature. Available as OTF/TTF under commercial or extended licence.

name: ARP3 Typeface
classification_notes: Geometric display face with sharp terminals contrasted by softened curves at stroke junctions. Clear futuristic/sci-fi aesthetic. Variable font included. 98-glyph character set limits it to strictly display use.
summary: A futuristic display face by Ciarán Brandin that pairs sharp terminals with softened stroke junctions, inspired by Floating Points' album Shadows.
description: ARP3 merges hard-edged letterforms with rounded transitions at the joints, producing a mechanical-yet-warm character well suited to headline and display work. Designed in 2019 and rooted in the sonic world of Floating Points, the family spans three weights – Thin, Regular and Heavy – each with a companion italic, plus a variable font. With 98 glyphs covering basic Latin, numbers and punctuation, the scope is deliberately narrow.
foundry_blurb: A futuristic typeface conceived alongside the Floating Points album Shadows, blending the warmth of analogue harmonics with the precision of electronic design. Sharp terminals meet softened curves at every letter joint, creating a distinctive hard-and-soft contrast. Available in OTF, TTF and web formats with variable font technology included.

name: Oddball TM
classification_notes: Single-weight handwritten display typeface with a deliberately imperfect, blob-like aesthetic. Three stylistic sets provide automatic glyph alternation for varied texture. 90s-inflected casual character throughout.
summary: A 90s-inspired handwritten display typeface with a deliberately imperfect, blob-like quality suited to casual, vintage-flavoured display work.
description: Oddball TM is a single-weight handwritten display font from Type Mania with a loose, blobby aesthetic drawn from 90s graphic culture. Its 589 glyphs include diacritics, ligatures, alternates, numbers, punctuation and currency, with three stylistic sets providing automatic variation. It covers the most popular Latin-based languages and is built for casual, retro or playful display applications.
foundry_blurb: Type Mania pitches Oddball TM as "perfectly imperfect" – a blob-y, 90s-inflected handwritten font that channels the energy of a favourite vintage band t-shirt. It ships with 589 glyphs, three stylistic sets with automatic alternation, and broad Latin language support, available as OTF, TTF and WOFF2 under commercial and extended licences.

name: Cavale V.2 Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight display serif with strict rectilinear (vertical and horizontal) serifs set against rounded letterforms. Described as fixed-width in character. Geometric contrast construction; themed around equestrian sport. No italics, no condensed, no additional weights.
summary: A fixed-width display serif built for equestrian contexts, pairing strict rectilinear serifs with rounded letterforms to produce something upright and a little haughty.
description: Cavale V.2 is a single-weight display typeface by Valentin Normand, conceived around equestrian sport. Its defining tension is structural: strict vertical and horizontal serifs set against rounded, curved letterforms – rigour and softness held in balance. At 202 glyphs it covers standard Latin alongside punctuation, currency and mathematical symbols, available in OTF and web formats.
foundry_blurb: Designed for equestrian sport, Cavale V.2 is described as proud, like a rider and their mount. The face contrasts geometric severity – strict vertical and horizontal serifs – with rounded letterforms, resulting in a fixed-width display type that carries both precision and a certain organic warmth.

name: SYNO MONO
classification_notes: Monospaced display typeface in two named cuts (SYNO MONO-I and SYNO MONO-2). 175 glyphs including uppercase, lowercase, figures, basic punctuation and multiple alternates. Aesthetic sits at the crossover between organic humanist form and rigid mechanical structure. No italic or condensed variants listed.
summary: A monospaced display typeface by Vienna-based designer Lukas Haider, available in two cuts and loaded with alternates that play the tension between organic form and mechanical rigidity.
description: SYNO MONO pairs strict monospacing with an expressive display sensibility, offering two distinct styles and 175 glyphs including multiple character alternates. The design sets fluid, humanist stroke qualities against the hard grid of a fixed-width system. It suits editorial headlines, logotypes and type-led graphic work where character takes priority over functional legibility.
foundry_blurb: A monospaced display typeface exploring the harmony between fluid human forms and the sharp precision of machinery. Available in two styles – SYNO MONO-I and SYNO MONO-2 – with 175 glyphs and multiple alternates. The commercial licence includes OTF; extended licences add WOFF and WOFF2.

name: Orion Typeface
classification_notes: Geometric display face with a deliberately angular, futuristic skeleton drawn from Greek letter forms. Hard diagonals and sharp terminals give it a sci-fi quality without falling into pure techno pastiche. Single weight, no italics, very limited glyph set (81 glyphs covering basic Latin, numerals and minimal punctuation).
summary: A single-weight cyberpunk display face by Paris-based designer Melvin Ghandour, built on Greek letter skeletons and originally drawn for a short film logotype.
description: Orion was designed in 2020 for the title card of the short film "Nostromo", with its skeleton borrowed from Greek letterforms and its aesthetic from cyberpunk fiction's collision of high technology and social decay. The result is a hard-edged, angular display face suited to headline or identity use in sci-fi and dystopian contexts. With 81 glyphs, a single weight and no italic, it is narrow in application by design.
foundry_blurb: Named for the mythological hunter turned constellation, Orion draws on the Greek alphabet's typographic skeleton and the cyberpunk subgenre's blend of futuristic technology and societal collapse. Available as OTF for commercial use, with WOFF and WOFF2 formats included in the extended licence.

name: Rosso Regular
classification_notes: Single-weight display face with bold, fluid letterforms drawn from the energy of dance movement. 82-glyph set covering basic Latin letters, numerals and punctuation. No alternates, ligatures or extended language support noted.
summary: A bold, single-weight display face by Lukas Haider that translates the fluid energy of dance into letterforms aimed at music and entertainment work.
description: Rosso Regular is a display typeface with expressive, movement-driven letterforms inspired by the dynamics of dance. Its 82-glyph set covers letters, numerals and basic punctuation, keeping it best suited to short-form headlines, posters and promotional material in music or entertainment contexts. At a single weight with no italics or alternates, the character palette is narrow but the personality is pronounced.
foundry_blurb: A display typeface inspired by the fluid, dynamic energy of dance movements – bold and expressive, and positioned as a versatile choice for music-related projects. Available as OTF under a commercial licence, with WOFF and WOFF2 formats added under the extended licence.

name: Wasp
classification_notes: Wide display typeface with Didone-derived stroke contrast and calligraphic swooshes, officially described by the foundry as a calligraphic humanist sans. The high-contrast strokes and ornamental flourishes place it firmly in display territory despite its sans-serif skeleton. Two weights only: Regular and Extra.
summary: A wide, high-contrast display sans from NaumType that borrows Didone stroke contrast and calligraphic swooshes for bold poster and editorial work.
description: Wasp is a wide display typeface built around non-conventional letter structures, sharp Didone-style contrast and expressive swoosh details that give it an ornamental edge. Designed by Peter Bushuev of NaumType, it sits in the territory between legible and decorative – suited to posters, album covers, packaging and oversized headlines where visual impact is the priority. The family covers 377 glyphs across a Latin European character set in two weights, Regular and Extra, with no italic or condensed companions.
foundry_blurb: A bold display typeface combining unconventional letter structures with classic Didone elements, high-contrast strokes and elegant swooshes. Covers 377 glyphs across the Latin European character set. Aimed at posters, album covers, branding, packaging and editorial layouts where the font needs to act as a visual centrepiece.

name: Loser TM
classification_notes: Bubbly, scribbled handwritten display face with bold rounded strokes. Single weight with two stylistic sets and automatic glyph alternation. Sits at the intersection of script and display – classified as display given its headline/logo-first intent and non-connecting letterforms.
summary: A scribbled, bubbly handwritten display face with automatic glyph alternation, pitched at social media graphics and quirky logo work.
description: Loser TM is a single-weight rounded display typeface from Type Mania, built around a deliberately rough, hand-scrawled aesthetic. Its 386-glyph set includes two stylistic sets with automatic alternation so repeated characters vary naturally. Latin coverage throughout; sold via 6TM Magazine's shop with commercial and extended licence options.
foundry_blurb: Type Mania's Loser TM is a bold, bubbly handwritten display font designed to help creatives stand out rather than blend in. The face targets social media graphics, quirky logos and personal branding, and ships as OTF, TTF and (on extended licence) WOFF2.

name: Dælort Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight serif with sharp, aggressively cut terminals and an elaborate ligature system; the overall dystopian aesthetic and display-only weight range place it in the display category rather than workhorse serif.
summary: A single-weight display serif by Jules Bigot with sharply aggressive terminals and a ligature-heavy construction drawn from a dystopian visual sensibility.
description: Dælort pairs a conventional serif skeleton with unconventional, sharply cut terminals that give each character a distinctly hostile edge. The typeface ships with 498 glyphs, three numeral sets and a ligature system designed to merge multiple letters into composite forms. With no italic or additional weight, it is best suited to editorial headlines and experimental display work where typographic personality carries the design.
foundry_blurb: The listing describes Dælort as a contemporary serif combining straight and curved lines with sharp, aggressive terminals inspired by a dystopian aesthetic. It includes a full Latin European character set, diacritics, multiple numeral sets, and ligatures that link letters to produce a unique typographic effect. Available in OTF for commercial use, or OTF, WOFF and WOFF2 under an extended licence.

name: QiGong V.06 Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight display typeface with deliberately distorted letterforms. Described as a derivative of QiGong V.01 (2020) by Kazuhiro Aihara. The design draws on martial arts movement and meditative restraint, producing organic irregularity rather than geometric precision. No italic, condensed or mono variants. Available in OTF with commercial and extended (OTF/WOFF/WOFF2) licences.
summary: A single-weight display face by Kazuhiro Aihara with deliberately distorted letterforms shaped by martial arts movement and meditative restraint – more art object than workhorse.
description: QiGong V.06 is a derivative of Aihara's earlier QiGong V.01 project, carrying forward its concept of typographic posture and graphic meditation. The letterforms are shaped by controlled distortion and spiritual restraint, evoking the discipline of traditional martial arts rather than conventional typographic construction. It suits art direction and editorial contexts where visual impact counts more than text legibility, though its single weight and narrow character set limit practical range.
foundry_blurb: A type system described as harmoniously displaying typographic posture, visual breathing and graphic meditation, with letterforms shaped by distortion and spiritual restraint inspired by traditional martial arts movements.

name: Briske
classification_notes: Single-weight connected display face where letterforms join to one another, giving a fluid, hand-lettered quality at large scales. Targeted at streetwear, apparel and poster work. Indie retail release with 110 glyphs covering basic Latin and extended characters.
summary: A single-weight connected display face by Jules Bigot, designed for streetwear graphics, album art and poster work.
description: Briske is a joined-letterform display typeface where each character flows into the next, creating a fluid, graffiti-adjacent energy suited to large-scale applications. Designed by Jules Bigot in 2022, it covers 110 glyphs across regular and extended Latin characters, numerals and punctuation. Its intended territory is clothing graphics, album artwork and poster design.
foundry_blurb: A bold display typeface with connected characters built for modern creative projects. Includes 110 glyphs — letters, extended characters, numbers and symbols — available in OTF under commercial or extended licence.

name: Mechanic Font
classification_notes: Single-weight industrial display typeface with heavy, angular sans-serif letterforms. The design leans into a grunge/cyberpunk aesthetic with boxy, bold strokes. Positioned purely for display and logo work, with no text weights, no italics and no condensed variants. Covers uppercase Latin, numerals and basic symbols only.
summary: A single-weight industrial display face with heavy, angular letterforms built for logo marks and display headlines.
description: Mechanic is a bold display typeface by hvnter, released in 2024 with a deliberate industrial character. The letterforms are angular and heavy, suiting logo marks, posters and signage where a strong, edgy presence matters. A single style covers uppercase Latin, numerals and basic symbols; there are no italics, no condensed variants and no text weights.
foundry_blurb: Described as a typeface with a subtle industrial theme, Mechanic pairs bold, boxy letterforms with a grunge edge. Available for personal and commercial use, it ships as a single OTF file covering the basic Latin alphabet, numerals and symbols.

name: 403 Cusion
classification_notes: Rounded, bulbous display type with no serifs and a distinctly inflated, "stuffed" quality to every stroke. Draws directly from 1970s advertising lettering – thick, soft curves, no harsh angles, optimistic in tone. Closer to groovy American photo-lettering of the period than geometric sans-serif.
summary: A chunky 1970s retro display face from 403TF, built on soft, rounded letterforms inspired by vintage upholstery and period advertising confidence.
description: 403 Cusion channels the visual language of 1970s advertising through thick, plush letterforms that feel almost tactile – rounded to the point of looking inflated, with none of the austerity of contemporary type. Two styles ship: Regular and Slant. The 732-glyph set covers alternates, ligatures, three numeral styles and extended punctuation, making it more considered than a typical novelty display release. It suits headlines, packaging, apparel and branding where a warm, retro optimism is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by the plush curves of vintage sofas and the unapologetic confidence of 70s advertising, 403 Cusion delivers groovy, rounded letterforms for expressive display use. Comes in Regular and Slant with 732 glyphs including alternates, ligatures and multiple numeral sets, available as OTF, TTF and web formats.

name: Nihilo Typeface
classification_notes: Bold display face with high contrast between thick main strokes and fine details, described as retro-inspired with a contemporary sensibility. Limited to 75 glyphs across a single weight. Available as OTF (commercial) and OTF/WOFF/WOFF2 (extended).
summary: A single-weight retro-modern display face by Noé Sainlez, built around high-contrast strokes and rounded curves with a deliberately limited 75-glyph character set.
description: Nihilo is a bold display typeface that draws on retro aesthetics while keeping a contemporary sensibility. High contrast between thick stems and fine details gives it visual character suited to headlines, logotypes and editorial work at large sizes. With 75 glyphs and one weight, it is a focused decorative tool rather than a workhorse.
foundry_blurb: A distinctive typeface combining a retro feel with a modern touch, built on bold thickness and beautiful curves. Covers uppercase, lowercase and numerals. Available with a commercial OTF licence or an extended licence that adds web formats.

name: Aether20 Typeface
classification_notes: Experimental display face with grid-based construction. Angular, acid-inflected letterforms on fixed proportions. Uppercase-only character set of 45 glyphs. Single weight, no stylistic alternates beyond select variants. Released at version 0.9.1.
summary: A single-weight experimental display face by Alex Ortiga, built on a rigid grid with sharp geometry and acid-inflected retro character.
description: Aether20 covers uppercase letters, figures and basic punctuation across 45 glyphs, with no italic, condensed or weight variants. It is built on a fixed grid that keeps proportions consistent across alignments. At version 0.9.1, it sits closer to a typographic experiment than a finished workhorse.
foundry_blurb: The listing describes Aether20 as combining sharp, dynamic letterforms with acid and minimalist retro aesthetics, constructed on a fixed grid for consistent proportions. It ships as OTF and, on the extended licence, WOFF and WOFF2, with select alternate characters included.

name: Lumen Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight geometric display drawn from photovoltaic panel patterns. A fixed x-height is shared between upper and lowercase; forms are organised around three axes to produce an orderly, rhythmic grid structure. Strong contrast between glyphs gives it a stable, technical presence.
summary: A single-weight geometric display face by Valentin Normand, structured around photovoltaic panel geometry for science and space-facing projects.
description: Lumen is a geometric display typeface built around the visual logic of photovoltaic panels. Upper and lowercase share a fixed x-height, and the letterforms are organised along three axes to create a grid-like regularity. With 292 glyphs including diacritics, symbols and mathematical characters, it is aimed squarely at science, research and future-oriented branding.
foundry_blurb: Sold on the 6TM Magazine shop as a commercial-licence OTF release. Described as designed for future-oriented projects in science, space exploration and research, with a structure drawing on solar panel geometry to produce "a strong, stable and subtle identity."

name: Esoteric Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight display serif drawing on illuminated manuscript and Roman capital traditions. Dramatic curves and decorative serifs position it firmly as a headline/editorial face. 203 glyphs covering Latin European characters with diacritics, plus stylistic alternates and ligatures. No italic, condensed, or mono variants offered.
summary: A single-weight display serif from Ben King, pairing the formality of Roman capitals with detailing drawn from illuminated manuscript traditions.
description: Esoteric Typeface combines the architectural weight of Roman capitals with decorative details borrowed from illuminated manuscripts, resulting in a distinctive headline face with dramatic curves and unconventional serifs. The single weight is supplemented by stylistic alternates and ligatures, giving designers some compositional flexibility. Coverage extends across the Latin European character set with diacritics, making it usable across Western European languages.
foundry_blurb: Contemporary display typeface characterised by dramatic curves and unique serifs, drawing influence from illuminated manuscripts and Roman capitals. Ships with 203 glyphs including a Latin European character set with diacritics, stylistic alternates, ligatures, full punctuation, numerals, symbols and currency marks. Available as OTF for commercial use, with web formats on the extended licence.

name: Polyphemus Typeface
classification_notes: A bold, single-weight display face drawing on mythology and 90s industrial aesthetics. Extremely limited character set of 26 glyphs (uppercase Latin only), making it purely decorative. No italics, no condensed, no mono.
summary: A bold, mythology-themed display face with a 90s industrial edge, limited to 26 uppercase glyphs and a single weight.
description: Polyphemus is a decorative display typeface inspired by the Cyclops of Greek myth, aiming to fuse ancient mythology with the raw industrial aesthetics of 1990s graphic design. It comprises just 26 uppercase glyphs, making it unsuitable for body text or extended typesetting. A novelty headline face with strong visual character but very narrow practical application.
foundry_blurb: A bold, one-eyed typeface inspired by the mythical giant son of Poseidon, blending the power of ancient mythology with the raw, edgy aesthetics of 90s industrial design.

name: Daruma 2.0 Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight decorative display face built from rounded tube-like strokes. The pipe/tube construction gives each letterform a three-dimensional, mechanical quality. Firmly in headline-only territory with no text-weight companion. 99-glyph coverage suggests basic Latin only.
summary: A single-weight tubular display face by Jules Bigot, its letterforms built from rounded pipe-like strokes designed for bold posters and book covers.
description: Daruma 2.0 is a decorative display typeface from French designer Jules Bigot, distinguishing itself through letterforms constructed from curved, tube-like strokes that lend each character a three-dimensional quality. With 99 glyphs covering the basic Latin alphabet, it is purpose-built for large-scale headline work on posters and covers. The distinctive pipe aesthetic is striking at display sizes but offers little flexibility beyond that context.
foundry_blurb: A contemporary display typeface with decorative curved characters made of tubes, positioned for eye-catching posters and book covers. Sold in OTF format under a commercial licence, with WOFF and WOFF2 formats added in the extended tier.

name: Bootzy TM
classification_notes: Bold rugged sans serif with a DIY/bootleg aesthetic and automatic stylistic alternation across three glyph sets; when identical characters appear consecutively the font cycles between variants to generate visual texture. Display-only, single weight, 407 glyphs covering extended Latin ranges.
summary: A heavy rugged sans serif with automatic glyph alternation that cycles through three stylistic sets when identical characters repeat consecutively.
description: Bootzy TM is a display typeface drawn from DIY bootleg culture, built as a heavy, rough-edged sans serif. Its defining feature is automatic stylistic alternation: when the same letter appears twice in a row, the font shifts between three glyph variants, generating visual texture without manual input. Suited to short-run display work – flyers, album covers, merchandise graphics – and has seen use in New York Times Magazine and Sziget Festival branding.
foundry_blurb: A tough sans serif built for high-impact display work. Bootzy TM uses three stylistic sets that alternate automatically when identical glyphs repeat, adding organic variety and texture to headlines and short copy. Covers Basic Latin and several extended Latin ranges, with 407 glyphs in total. Available in OTF, TTF and WOFF2.

name: Neobleed Typeface
classification_notes: Modular blackletter display face. Draws explicitly from Gothic/blackletter script tradition, retaining characteristic lowercase serifs. Single weight, 70 glyphs covering basic Latin letters, numerals and punctuation. No italic, condensed or mono variants.
summary: A modular blackletter display face by Melvin Ghandour that applies a geometric grid to Gothic script conventions, leaning into the raw drama rather than softening it.
description: Neobleed takes modular construction and maps it onto blackletter tradition, keeping the characteristic lowercase serifs of Gothic scripts while stripping away any historical reverence. The design presents itself as raw and complex by intent, treating the dark connotations of the Gothic label as a feature. At 70 glyphs covering basic Latin, numerals and punctuation, it is strictly a display face with narrow practical range.
foundry_blurb: A modular typeface inspired by blackletter and Gothic script that leans into the aesthetic's raw, complex and dramatic qualities rather than rehabilitating them. Available as OTF for commercial use, with web formats included in the extended licence.

name: Resident Typeface
classification_notes: Pixel-grid modular display family with five stylistic cuts (Round, Bubble, Pixel, Horizontal Barcode, Vertical Barcode). Each cut is a distinct visual interpretation of the same modular skeleton. No italic, no condensed, no mono. Rooted in techno poster work from Bern 2022–2023. Purely a display typeface with no text-setting ambitions.
summary: A five-cut modular display family grown from Swiss techno poster work, with each cut offering a distinct filter on the same pixel-grid skeleton.
description: Resident Typeface comes from a series of techno posters Tobias Bolliger (Studio Bollo) made in Bern between 2022 and 2023. The family shares a single modular grid skeleton, then diverges into five cuts – Round, Bubble, Pixel, Horizontal Barcode and Vertical Barcode – through component modifications and visual filters. Each cut ships with 264 glyphs covering upper and lowercase, figures, punctuation, currency, arrows and symbols; the full package runs to 1,320 glyphs.
foundry_blurb: Resident Typeface is a modular, pixel-grid-based font family created from a series of techno posters presented in Bern, Switzerland, between 2022 and 2023. It uses modifications of components and a range of filters across five cuts to achieve diverse visual variations, available as a family or as individual styles.

name: Pressed Flaws Font
classification_notes: Display typeface with a distressed grunge aesthetic, evoking aged letterpress printing and typewriter wear. Two weights, 204-glyph Latin set. No extended language support indicated.
summary: A two-weight distressed display face with grungy, uneven edges designed to suggest aged printing or typewriter wear, aimed at posters, album covers and branding.
description: Pressed Flaws draws on the visual language of worn letterpress and old typewriters, applying an irregular, textured treatment to a basic Latin set across two weights. The raw, industrial aesthetic is pitched at posters, album artwork, packaging and street-inspired design. At 204 glyphs it covers standard Latin letters, numerals, punctuation and currency, with no extended language or variant support.
foundry_blurb: Designed to replicate worn-out printing, this textured font features grungy, uneven edges that add depth and a handcrafted feel. Recommended for editorial layouts, branding, music visuals and any project requiring an edgy or aged print aesthetic.

name: Cascadeur
classification_notes: Modular sans-serif constructed on a 4-line grid with a space-age, modernist aesthetic. Offers 2–4 alternates per letter. Available as a variable font with weight, slant and roundness axes, plus static Round and standard subfamilies each with oblique styles. No true italics; obliques only.
summary: A grid-based modular sans with space-age character, five weights, a Round subfamily, oblique styles and a variable font covering weight, slant and roundness axes.
description: Cascadeur is a modular sans-serif built on a strict 4-line grid, drawing on space-age and modernist type traditions. Each weight ships with oblique and Round variants, and a variable font exposes three axes – weight, slant and roundness – giving considerable flexibility for headline and display work. With 756 glyphs, multiple alternates per letter and full Cyrillic coverage, it is better resourced than most indie display releases.
foundry_blurb: Designed by Naum Type, Cascadeur is a modular sans built on a 4-line grid with inventive letterforms drawn from space-age and modernist traditions. It includes 12 static styles with oblique variants, a mirrored Round subfamily and a variable font with weight, slant and roundness axes. Suited to posters, album covers, editorial headlines, identity and packaging.

name: FYE
classification_notes: Experimental display face with organic letterforms derived from butterfly wing patterns; covers only the 26 basic Latin letters with no numerals, punctuation or extended characters.
summary: FYE is a 26-letter display face by Awista, drawing its letterforms from butterfly wing patterns for short, visually striking headlines.
description: Designed by Awista, FYE derives its letterforms from the intricate markings of butterfly wings, giving the face an organic, irregular quality that is firmly display-only. With just 26 glyphs covering the basic alphabet and no numerals or punctuation, its character coverage is very limited. Best suited to single words or short phrases where visual texture outweighs legibility.
foundry_blurb: FYE is an experimental typeface developed from close study of butterfly wing patterns. The designer cropped and abstracted natural markings to produce distinctive letterforms intended to create captivating phrases when set together.

name: Buzzer TM
classification_notes: A single-weight distressed sans-serif display face with a vibrating, grunge-adjacent aesthetic. Tags include vintage, punk, 90s and gritty. Released June 2024 by Type Mania. Sold via multiple resellers including 6TM Magazine, Creative Market and Pixel Surplus.
summary: A distressed, jazzy single-weight sans-serif display face built for high-energy print work like gig posters and flyers.
description: Buzzer TM leans hard into a vibrating, distressed aesthetic that suits loud, attention-demanding print contexts. Its 186-glyph set covers Basic Latin alongside Central European and Pan African Latin scripts. Narrow in application but effective within its lane, it is a solid pick for designers who need instant attitude in a headline.
foundry_blurb: A jazzy sans-serif described as guaranteed to electrify text with energy and excitement. Positioned for flyers, posters and any attention-demanding gig, it comes in OTF, TTF and WOFF2 formats under commercial and extended licence options.

name: Bizkea
classification_notes: Garalde-influenced display serif with classical proportions and details pushed towards a modern aesthetic. Single weight, no italics or condensed variants. 400+ glyphs including ligatures, stylistic alternates and three numeral sets. Positioned for large-size headline and branding use.
summary: A single-weight Garalde-influenced display serif from Indonesian designer Ahmad Nur Alfian, aimed at elegant branding, poster work and logo design.
description: Bizkea draws on the proportions and detailing of classical Garalde serifs, reinterpreted for contemporary display use. It is designed primarily for large-size headings, titles and branding contexts where its historical character reads clearly. The Latin European character set includes ligatures, stylistic alternates and three numeral sets.
foundry_blurb: A display serif blending classical Garalde elegance with a modern approach. Suited to elegant branding, vintage-inspired graphic design, posters, logos and album covers. Available in OTF and TTF formats under a commercial licence, with WOFF and WOFF2 added at the extended tier.

name: Grundtvig Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight monospaced display typeface. Bold, angular letterforms with strong verticality derived from the stepped gabled facade and pointed arches of Grundtvig Kirke, Copenhagen. Pixel-adjacent rigidity sits between gothic revival and bitmap aesthetics. Not a text face — built purely for headlines and prominent typographic use.
summary: A single-weight monospaced display face drawn from the angular geometry of Grundtvig Kirke in Copenhagen, designed as a student project at ELISAVA in 2023.
description: Grundtvig takes its letterforms from the stepped gabled facade and pointed arches of Copenhagen's Grundtvig Kirke. Designed by Reinaldo Camejo during a master's in Visual Design at ELISAVA, it is a monospaced display face built for headlines and prominent typographic use. The forms are bold and architectural, with a pixel-adjacent rigidity that recalls bitmap type as much as gothic revival – and has collected awards from ADC Young Ones, ADG Laus and LAD.
foundry_blurb: An experimental typeface inspired by the distinctive elements of the iconic west facade of Grundtvig Kirke in Copenhagen. Drawing from the building's verticality, stepped gable contours and doorway arches, it takes contemporary graphic form rather than traditional gothic styling. Supports Latin European languages with 150 glyphs including diacritics, numbers, punctuation and symbols. Available in OTF; extended licence adds WOFF and WOFF2.

name: Moslin
classification_notes: Single-weight hand-drawn display face with loose, casual letterforms. Produced with Fontself Maker 3.5.7. Latin script only, no italic, condensed or mono variants.
summary: A single-weight hand-drawn display face from indie designer Hvnter, with a loose, casual character pitched at informal branding and poster work.
description: Moslin is a hand-lettered display typeface offering one weight in a relaxed, slightly rough style. The glyph set covers uppercase, lowercase, numerals and basic symbols, with a handful of bonus alternates. It suits informal branding, posters and creative projects where a personal, handcrafted feel matters more than typographic rigour.
foundry_blurb: Moslin is described as a hand-drawn typeface with relaxed, stylish charm and a cool, effortless vibe. The foundry pitches it as bringing character and warmth to designs with a playful yet polished touch, targeting branding, posters and general creative projects.

name: Croissant Display
classification_notes: Single-weight display font with centripetal letterforms – each character draws inward toward its own centre. The design concept references the Axis Mundi, blending symbolic geometry with industrial and digital aesthetics. Not a conventional display cut; the centripetal structure limits legibility at smaller sizes and restricts versatility.
summary: A single-weight display typeface in which each letterform converges inward toward its own centre, drawn from the symbolic concept of the Axis Mundi.
description: Croissant Display is built around a centripetal structural conceit – letterforms that draw inward toward their own centre, giving the type a gravitational, almost hypnotic quality. The design takes the Axis Mundi as its conceptual anchor, merging symbolic geometry with industrial and digital influences. With 189 glyphs including alternates, it suits short display runs and headline contexts where visual distinctiveness matters more than readability.
foundry_blurb: A self-centred typeface where characters elegantly converge toward their own centre, inspired by the symbolic Axis Mundi. It merges ancient meaning with industrial and digital influences, creating a balance between timeless symbolism and modern design. Includes 189 glyphs across letters, alternates, numbers, punctuation, symbols, currency and arrows.

name: Basic TM
classification_notes: Single-weight display typeface built on ASCII and early computing references. Blocky, grid-constrained letterforms designed for headline and decorative use only. No text-size utility.
summary: A single-weight ASCII-inspired display face by Type Mania, channelling early computing aesthetics for flyers, event collateral and retro-digital headlines.
description: Basic TM draws on ASCII terminal letterforms to produce a deliberately lo-fi display typeface with grid-constrained construction. It covers Basic Latin and extends to Central European and Pan African Latin, with 193 glyphs in a single weight. Best suited to short-burst headline and poster work where the retro-computing reference is the point.
foundry_blurb: Basic TM brings the nostalgia of early computing into the 2020s with a twist. Whether you're designing a flyer for an underground dance party or crafting a quirky advertisement, it delivers undeniable style to any project.

name: Vertig Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight display face with neo-retro styling by Jules Bigot (Big Concrete Planet). Described as inspired by "enigmatic futuristic script." 87 glyphs covering letters, numerals and basic punctuation. Suited only to headline and title use; not a text face. No italic, condensed or mono variants.
summary: A single-weight neo-retro display face by Jules Bigot, with detailed decorative letterforms built for headlines and editorial titles.
description: Vertig is a decorative display typeface sitting somewhere between retro and futuristic, designed for titles and headlines rather than body text. Its 87 glyphs cover the essentials – letters, numerals and basic punctuation – at a single weight with detailed, eye-catching character shapes. It is a niche choice, best suited to short-burst editorial or branding contexts where visual impact takes precedence over versatility.
foundry_blurb: The listing describes Vertig as a neo-retro typeface inspired by enigmatic futuristic script, with captivating detailed characters designed to produce elegant titles and striking headlines.

name: Mikon
classification_notes: Single-weight geometric display face with capsule-shaped, heavily rounded terminals throughout.
