The rounded stroke endings give it a soft, inflated quality distinct from traditional rounded sans-serifs. No stress axis visible; uniform stroke weight with a geometric construction. Futuristic in character rather than retro.
summary: A single-weight geometric display face by Paris-based designer Dae Huen Lee, built around capsule-shaped rounded terminals inspired by levitating pod vehicles.
description: Mikon is a bold display typeface with uniformly rounded, capsule-shaped stroke endings that give it a soft, slightly inflated futuristic quality. Designed for headlines, logos and graphic applications, it covers Latin European languages across 382 glyphs – including ligatures, alternates, four numeral sets and prebuilt fractions. The designer, Dae Huen Lee (QUICKNAP.ZZZ), studied typography at École Estienne in Paris, and the technical implementation reflects that training.
foundry_blurb: Mikon is a bold display typeface with capsule-shaped rounded edges drawn from the aesthetic of levitating pod transportation. Suited to logos, graphics and headlines, it ships with 382 glyphs covering Latin European languages, alongside ligatures, alternates and multiple numeral styles. Available as OTF and TTF for commercial use, with web formats included in the extended licence.

name: Dreamer TM
classification_notes: Emotive display serif with Y2K styling. Single weight with two stylistic sets, ligatures and alternates across 336 glyphs. Designed explicitly for headline and logo use, not body text.
summary: A Y2K-inflected display serif with two stylistic sets and decorative alternates, aimed at posters, logos and nostalgic branding.
description: Dreamer TM is an emotive display serif drawing on Y2K nostalgia, featuring edgy vintage letterforms with decorative Unicode symbols. It ships as a single weight with two stylistic sets for automatic glyph alternation, plus ligatures and alternates across 336 characters. Positioned for headline and logo contexts rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: An emotive serif with Y2K character, covering 336 glyphs including stylistic sets, ligatures and alternates. Suited to posters, logo design and nostalgia-driven branding work.

name: Dearbomb Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight display face where each character is constructed as an asymmetric sculptural silhouette, playing with light and shadow. Letterforms are treated as independent abstract forms rather than conventional glyphs. Avant-garde fashion and modernist sculpture are cited as the primary references (Yohji Yamamoto, Isamu Noguchi).
summary: A single-weight display face by Morgane Pierra Andrée that builds each glyph as an asymmetric sculptural silhouette, channelling Yohji Yamamoto and Isamu Noguchi into type.
description: Dearbomb treats letterforms as abstract sculptural objects, each one an asymmetric silhouette that plays light against shadow. The 160-glyph set covers Latin Extended characters with diacritics, numerals and punctuation, giving it enough range for European headline use. It is best suited to posters and editorial contexts where an expressive, fashion-inflected display face is the point – not a workhorse font.
foundry_blurb: Described as a dualistic display typeface inspired by the work of Yohji Yamamoto and the sculptural forms of Isamu Noguchi, with each character conceived as an asymmetric sculptural silhouette. Sold at €22 as an OTF commercial licence, with WOFF and WOFF2 formats added at the extended licence tier.

name: Hotdex
classification_notes: Single-weight bold organic display face with oversized letterforms, generous curves and a fluid rhythm. No weights, no italics, no condensed variants. Headline and poster use only.
summary: A single-weight organic display face from French designer Jonathan Grzywinski, built on oversized letterforms and fluid curves aimed at headline and poster work.
description: Hotdex is a bold organic display typeface with generous curves and an oversized character that gives it a fluid, eye-catching quality. It's intended for attention-grabbing headlines, posters and branding contexts where typographic personality matters more than versatility. With 160 glyphs and diacritic support it covers Western European Latin scripts, but the single-weight, no-italic format limits its range considerably.
foundry_blurb: Hotdex is described as a bold and expressive typeface with generous curves, an organic rhythm and oversized characters that deliver a fluid yet powerful visual impact. The listing positions it for attention-grabbing headlines, posters and bold branding projects.

name: Sonic Fraktur
classification_notes: Single-weight blackletter in the fraktur tradition, reinterpreted with sharp, industrial edges and an acid aesthetic. Limited to 36 glyphs covering basic Latin letters and numerals. Display-only use case with no text weight or extended character support.
summary: A sharp-edged single-weight blackletter by Alexander Raffl, designed for logos, posters and album covers with an industrial, acid-tinged aesthetic.
description: Sonic Fraktur applies fraktur forms to a bold, industrial design language – sharp edges and a deliberately confrontational look. Its 36-glyph set covers basic Latin letters and numerals only, limiting it to short headline work. Best used where attitude matters more than typographic breadth.
foundry_blurb: Combines sharp edges and a bold aesthetic for a cutting-edge look that demands attention. Designed for acid, industrial and futuristic projects – logos, posters, album covers and digital artwork.

name: Quiet Attempt Soft Handwritten Script
classification_notes: Casual handwritten script with deliberately trembling strokes and variable ink flow. Single weight, organic letterforms, 199 glyphs covering Latin European languages. No italic or condensed variants – the oblique quality is inherent to the design.
summary: A single-weight casual handwritten script by Victoria Strukovskaya, built around trembling strokes and gentle ink flow for intimate branding, wedding stationery and editorial work.
description: Quiet Attempt is a soft handwritten script with 199 glyphs covering Latin European languages. Its deliberately imperfect letterforms – trembling strokes and variable ink weight – suit wedding stationery, café signage, packaging and social graphics where warmth matters more than precision. Available as OTF, TTF, WOFF and WOFF2 under commercial and extended licences.
foundry_blurb: Designed to feel personal and human, Quiet Attempt balances romance with vulnerability through organic letterforms and subtle irregularities. The shop pitches it for intimate branding, editorial layouts, packaging and social media visuals – anywhere that calls for expressive personality over geometric polish.

name: 403 Mono
classification_notes: Variable monospaced typeface with geometric/grotesque construction; seven upright weights, no italics or condensed variants; designed for code and interface use.
summary: A clean geometric mono spanning seven weights with variable technology, built for code editors and digital interfaces.
description: 403 Mono is a variable monospaced typeface from 403TF, running from Light to Black across seven weights. Its geometry is consistent and utilitarian, well-suited to code environments and UI work. The 671-glyph set covers diacritics, ligatures, currency symbols and mathematical notation.
foundry_blurb: 403 Mono is pitched as a versatile monospaced typeface with clean lines, consistent character widths and variable weight control. It ships with OpenType features including ligatures and alternates, and is available in OTF, TTF, WOFF and WOFF2 formats depending on licence tier.

name: Base&Bloom
subcategory: Geometric display sans with calligraphic flourishes
classification_notes: Monoline geometric sans skeleton fused with high-contrast Didone-style swashes integrated structurally into the letterforms. Single weight with 7 stylistic sets and up to 11 alternates per glyph, covering 1,257 glyphs total. Latin European and Cyrillic character sets.
summary: A single-weight experimental display sans that grafts high-contrast Didone swashes onto a geometric monoline structure, with 1,257 glyphs, seven stylistic sets and up to 11 alternates per glyph.
description: Base&Bloom fuses a geometric monoline sans skeleton with ornate high-contrast flourishes, treating swashes as structural elements rather than decorative additions. The result ranges from a techno script to a brutalist grotesque depending on which stylistic set you draw on. It suits posters, album covers, packaging and editorial headlines; it is not a text face.
foundry_blurb: An experimental fusion of geometric monoline sans and high-contrast Didone flourishes, reimagining swashes as integral letterform elements rather than accessories. With 1,257 glyphs, seven stylistic sets and up to 11 alternates per letter, the typeface can shift between an exquisite techno script and a stout brutalist grotesque. Supports Latin European and Cyrillic.

name: Botch
classification_notes: Single-weight hand-drawn display face. Bubbly, rounded letterforms with a deliberately imperfect, analog-grunge character — somewhere between bubble lettering and DIY zine typography. 99 glyphs covering basic Latin only.
summary: A single-weight hand-drawn display face with bubbly, feral letterforms suited to punk posters, rave flyers and bootleg branding.
description: Botch is a hand-drawn display typeface by HVNTER with rounded, warped letterforms that sit somewhere between bubble lettering and deliberate imperfection. Its 99 glyphs cover uppercase, lowercase, numerals and basic punctuation. Best suited to zines, streetwear graphics and poster work where analog weirdness is an asset.
foundry_blurb: A feral, cheerfully imperfect display face from HVNTER. Bubbly organic letterforms with a grunge-DIY edge, positioned for logo work, packaging and branding that wants warmth over polish. Available as OTF in commercial and extended licences.

name: So Pretty Typeface
classification_notes: Single-weight hand-drawn script. Thin strokes with deliberately jagged, imperfect edges intended to convey intimacy and vulnerability. Romantic in character; firmly a display face for headlines and branding rather than body text.
summary: A single-weight hand-drawn romantic script with thin, deliberately uneven strokes, pitched at beauty branding, editorial layouts and poetic visual identities.
description: So Pretty is a delicate hand-drawn script by Softulka, built around thin strokes with intentionally rough, imperfect edges that give it an intimate, human quality. The 192-glyph set covers upper and lowercase letters, diacritics, numerals and symbols, offering reasonable coverage for European languages. It suits fashion and beauty branding, album artwork and editorial work where a gentle, lyrical aesthetic is the goal.
foundry_blurb: An intentionally shy and raw hand-drawn romantic script with thin, delicate lines and slightly jagged edges designed to evoke a vulnerable, human feel. Supplied in OTF and TTF formats (WOFF included on extended licence), with 192 glyphs covering diacritics, currency, punctuation and mathematical symbols.

name: Oldforge Distressed Font
classification_notes: Single-style decorative display face with heavy distressing throughout and medieval manuscript influences. Irregular stroke endings and worn texture define the character rather than any strict blackletter structure, placing it squarely in display rather than blackletter. Creative Market lists it as "Script" but the letterforms and intended use are firmly display-oriented.
summary: A single-weight medieval display face by Softulka, built on distressed texture and deliberately irregular letterforms aimed at titles, game design and historical branding.
description: Oldforge takes its cues from worn manuscripts and hand-forged metalwork, giving each letterform uneven edges and a weathered, pitted texture throughout. It ships as one weight with 191 glyphs covering standard Latin, punctuation, numbers and basic symbols. The distressing is consistent rather than random, making it readable at headline sizes but limiting its range to purely decorative settings.
foundry_blurb: A medieval-inspired distressed typeface with irregular lines, rugged curves and natural imperfections designed to evoke worn manuscripts and hand-forged artefacts. Suited to posters, book covers, game design, packaging and any display work requiring a historical or fantasy aesthetic.

name: Peace TM
classification_notes: Single-weight informal handwritten script inspired by 1960s American underground comic lettering. Features two OpenType stylistic sets that alternate automatically between glyph variants. No condensed, italic or mono companions.
summary: A single-weight handwritten script channelling 1960s underground comic lettering, with two stylistic sets that alternate automatically for varied glyph shapes.
description: Peace TM draws on the informal, expressive lettering of 1960s underground comics, with a restless hand-drawn quality suited to retro editorial and poster work. A single weight carries two stylistic sets that toggle automatically via OpenType, producing glyph variation without manual intervention. The 390-glyph set covers uppercase, lowercase, diacritics, ligatures and standard punctuation.
foundry_blurb: A handwritten typeface inspired by the underground comics of the 1960s, programmed to shift automatically between two stylistic sets to keep layouts dynamic. Aimed at graphic designers, artists and enthusiasts of the period.

name: 403 Vusion
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with a variable width axis spanning 12 widths from XXX Squeezed to Wide. Oblique (slant) styles are provided per width rather than true italics with distinct letterform design. No separate weight axis – width is the primary design variable, with all instances at a single implied weight.
summary: A variable-width geometric sans-serif from Indonesian foundry 403TF, spanning 12 widths and 24 named styles for branding, UI and high-impact editorial work.
description: 403 Vusion is a variable-width geometric sans from Indonesian foundry 403TF, offering 24 named instances across 12 widths – each available in regular and oblique cuts. The geometric construction keeps it legible at smaller sizes, while the width range from XXX Squeezed to Wide gives layouts significant expressive reach. At 750+ glyphs per style with 100+ language support, it covers most Latin-script projects without supplementary fonts.
foundry_blurb: Pitched as a high-utility contemporary sans for branding, UI/UX, packaging and editorial work. The foundry describes it as combining razor-sharp geometric lines with a hard-edged presence suited to high-tech interfaces, streetwear branding and anything requiring visual authority.

name: 403 Code Fuzz
designer: Umar Al Farouq, Jodi El Ghazi, Febri Riansah
classification_notes: Industrial stencil display face with strict octagonal construction and chamfered edges. Draws on military signage, vintage data terminals and sports jersey lettering. Strictly display-weight; two styles only – Regular and an oblique Slant.
summary: A cyber-brutalist stencil display face built on strict octagonal geometry, designed for streetwear branding and heavy industrial applications.
description: 403 Code Fuzz pairs chamfered, block letterforms with a military-stencil aesthetic drawn from vintage data terminals and logistics signage. Two styles – Regular for blunt authority, Slant for forward lean – cover the expected display range. With 707 glyphs and Latin coverage across 332 languages, it has more practical reach than most novelty display faces.
foundry_blurb: Billed as a typographic weapon for the modern industrialist, built on strict octagonal construction with chamfered edges drawn from military stencils and vintage sports jerseys. Designed to feel engineered rather than drawn, targeting streetwear branding, brutalist web interfaces, and high-impact display work.

name: Pasta Monday Pixel Script
classification_notes: 8-bit pixel-grid script with connected letterforms; decorative display face drawing on arcade culture and vintage signage. Despite the "script" label in its name, the pixel construction places it firmly in the display/novelty category.
summary: A pixel-grid script built on 8-bit arcade nostalgia, with connected letterforms suited to posters, album art and craft-adjacent display work.
description: The Native Saint Club renders a connected script entirely through pixel grids, landing somewhere between retro gaming and decorative display lettering. It ships with 551 glyphs, two stylistic sets and thorough punctuation coverage – solid for a single-weight novelty release. Best used large, where the pixel construction reads as a deliberate aesthetic choice rather than a limitation.
foundry_blurb: A pixel-crafted script blending 8-bit aesthetics with decorative, handcrafted character. Pitched at posters, album artwork, branding, craft-inspired graphics and cross-stitch-style designs. Available commercially in OTF and TTF; extended licence adds WOFF and WOFF2.

name: Black Mamba Typeface
classification_notes: A single-style monospace display face with an extremely limited character set of 26 uppercase glyphs only. No weight or width variations. Fixed-width spacing with decorative, sinuous letterforms. Purely ornamental in function.
summary: A 26-glyph monospace display face by Awista, drawing on the agility of Kobe Bryant and the Black Mamba snake for short-burst decorative headlines.
description: Black Mamba is a single-style display monospace with only 26 uppercase letters, designed by Awista to evoke the dynamism of basketball legend Kobe Bryant and the snake that gave him his nickname. The letterforms aim for a sinuous, fluid quality suited to sports-adjacent branding and headline use. Its extremely limited glyph set means it functions purely as decoration, with no capacity for continuous text.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by Kobe Bryant and the Black Mamba snake, the typeface sets out to be dynamic, sinuous and unstoppable. Sold with Commercial and Extended licences; the Extended tier adds WOFF and WOFF2 web formats alongside the TTF.

name: Malcom
classification_notes: Single-weight heavy display face with a contemporary, slightly playful character. Notable for 50+ letter alternates across a 157-glyph set. No weight range, no italic, no condensed. Aimed at logo and branding use rather than text setting.
summary: A bold, single-weight display face with 50-plus letter alternates, built for logo and brand identity work.
description: Malcom is a heavy display typeface with a contemporary, slightly playful character. Its 157-glyph set includes over 50 letter alternates, giving designers flexibility when setting logotypes or bespoke lettering. It ships in OTF format with a commercial licence, with web formats available on an extended licence.
foundry_blurb: A bold, heavy display font designed for modern clean visuals, featuring over 50 letter variations across 157 glyphs — suited to logos, brand identities and custom lettering projects.

name: Altotype
classification_notes: Single-weight rounded display typeface with heavy, uniform curves throughout. Features multiple glyph alternates per letter rather than optical size or weight variation. Closest to a geometric display with exaggerated roundness — sits in display rather than sans-serif because it is decorative-first.
summary: A single-weight rounded display face from Perth-based designer Hvnter, offering per-letter alternates to vary compositions in logo and editorial settings.
description: Altotype is a bold, heavily rounded display typeface designed for headline and identity work. It ships with 183 glyphs including A–Z, numerals and basic symbols, plus multiple alternates per letter to give designers variation without switching fonts. There is one weight and no italic or condensed cut; the appeal is the consistency of the rounded forms and the flexibility the alternates provide.
foundry_blurb: A display typeface built around heavily rounded characters, with multiple variations for each letter to open up creative possibilities in identity, editorial and type-based logo work. Available in OTF for commercial use, with WOFF and WOFF2 formats included in the extended licence.

name: Strikt
classification_notes: Built entirely on a 3x3 grid; every stroke derived from the same square unit. Two variable axes: weight and animation. The animation axis morphs glyphs into dot arrays, making this as much a motion tool as a typeface. Very limited character set (88 glyphs). Designed for display and kinetic use only – unsuitable for text setting.
summary: A modular variable display typeface built on a 3×3 grid, with an animation axis that morphs each glyph into a dot array – designed primarily for kinetic typography and motion work.
description: Designed by Peter Bushuev under the NAUM Type banner and released in 2020, Strikt ships across two subfamilies – standard and Plus – spanning Hairline to Extra Black via a variable weight axis. The Plus variant adds a harder sci-fi and techno character, enabling seamless dot-grid transitions between glyphs. Best suited to motion graphics, posters and experimental identities; its 88-glyph character set and strict modular construction rule out text setting.
foundry_blurb: A variable modular font built on a 3x3 grid with two axes – weight and animation. The animation axis transforms each glyph into a dot array and back, making it ready for kinetic typography, motion graphics and experimental design. The Plus version adds consistent dot arrays across all glyphs for seamless character-to-character transitions with a sci-fi and techno feel.

name: Counter
classification_notes: Variable display typeface built around an extreme inktrap concept. The design uses a single variable axis toggling between intact letterforms (Normal) and letterforms broken at inktrap stress points (Inktrap). Lowercase-only, 30 glyphs. No serifs; the broken forms give an almost deconstructed sans-serif appearance.
summary: A variable display typeface by Marco Rollo that exaggerates inktraps until they fracture the letterforms, delivered as a 30-glyph, lowercase-only font with two states.
description: Counter takes the inktrap – a notch originally cut into letterforms to compensate for ink spread – and pushes it to breaking point, splitting the characters open at stress areas. The variable axis moves between Normal (intact) and Inktrap (fractured), giving it a distinctive split-personality effect. With only 30 lowercase glyphs it is strictly a display tool, best suited to single-word logos, titles and motion design.
foundry_blurb: Counter is a variable display font composed exclusively of lowercase letters, built around an extreme reinterpretation of inktraps. Where conventional inktraps are subtle corrections, here they are pushed until they break the letterform apart entirely. The font ships in TTF (and WOFF/WOFF2 on the extended licence) and is positioned for logos, headlines and motion design work.

name: 403 Astona
classification_notes: High-contrast geometric sans-serif with brutalist industrial character. Variable weight axis spanning Thin to Black, released in Standard, Slant and Soft variants per weight. Explicitly positioned as a display typeface for headlines and tech-wear branding rather than text setting.
summary: A techno display sans from Indonesian foundry 403TF, built on high-contrast geometry and brutalist industrial references across 24 styles.
description: 403 Astona draws on trail running gear and industrial labelling for its visual logic – rigid geometry, experimental letterforms and a weight axis running from Thin to Black. Each weight ships in Standard, Slant and Soft variants, giving fine control over tone without losing the typeface's core character. Best suited to tech-wear branding, display editorial work and UI headlines.
foundry_blurb: Positioned by the studio as built for the intersection of high-performance utility and brutalist aesthetics, 403 Astona pairs industrial strength with futuristic geometry. Twenty-four styles cover six weights across Standard, Slant and Soft variants, supported by 870 glyphs per style, five numeral sets and coverage for over 340 languages.

name: Radiate
classification_notes: Experimental display font built around abstract rotation and unconventional letter structures. Two structural subfamilies — Open and Mesh — each spanning six weights. Letterforms prioritise visual impact and motion over legibility, with 94 glyphs covering basic Latin.
summary: Radiate is an experimental display font by Jason Santos built around abstract, rotational letterforms, offered in Open and Mesh variants across six weights.
description: Built around abstracted, rotational letterforms, Radiate treats type as a visual object rather than a reading tool. It comes in two structural variants — Open and Mesh — each spanning six weights from Regular to Black. Best suited to avant-garde branding, fashion editorial, album packaging and poster work where typographic impact matters more than legibility.
foundry_blurb: Radiate uses fluid movement and abstract rotation as its formal premise, with unconventional letter structures intended to give typography a futuristic, artistic character. The family ships in OTF and TTF for commercial licences, with WOFF and WOFF2 added on the extended licence.

name: New Phase
classification_notes: Display serif where each glyph is constructed from repeating vertical stripes of varying heights. The letterforms retain a serif skeleton but the interior strokes are replaced with stacked vertical columns, creating a textural, architectural quality. Single weight; clearly designed for large-scale headline use.
summary: A single-weight display serif by Softulka in which every glyph is constructed from repeating vertical stripes of varying heights, producing a textural, architecturally-inflected typeface built for large-scale headline use.
description: New Phase takes a classical serif skeleton and rebuilds each character from columns of vertical stripes at varying heights – a construction that reads as graphic pattern at distance and letterform up close. The effect suits posters, covers and campaign headlines, where the optical movement the striping generates becomes part of the composition. At text sizes the concept collapses; this is a typeface designed to be seen large.
foundry_blurb: An experimental display serif inspired by medieval inscriptions and monumental stone carvings. Each character is constructed from repeating vertical stripes of varying heights, creating what the designer describes as a balance between historical elegance and modern visual experimentation. Suited to branding, luxury packaging, book covers, magazine layouts, posters and fashion campaigns.

name: Crash TM
classification_notes: A single-weight distressed display sans-serif with three OpenType stylistic sets that cycle automatically in a 1-2-3 pattern, producing organic variation across repeated glyphs. The base letterforms are sans-serif but the primary intent is novelty display use.
summary: A distressed display sans-serif that cycles through three stylistic alternates automatically, built for raw, energetic headline use.
description: Crash TM uses OpenType stylistic sets to rotate through three distressed variants in a 1-2-3 pattern, giving layouts an organic, hand-worn quality without manual alternates. The letterforms are bold and impact-driven, suited to posters, event flyers and branding with a street or underground tone. It ships as a single weight with 588 glyphs covering major Latin-based scripts.
foundry_blurb: A rugged display typeface that automatically cycles through three stylistic sets, offering fresh variation with each character. Created by Type Mania, it comes in OTF, TTF and WOFF2 formats under commercial or extended licence.

name: Chunk Chonk Typeface
classification_notes: Ultra-heavy brutalist display face with two geometric subfamilies: Square (angular) and Round (softened corners). Uppercase-only with 68 glyphs. No lowercase, no italics. Basic Latin only.
summary: A blocky, ultra-heavy display face by Jason Santos in two geometric styles – Square and Round – each available at three weights, aimed at streetwear, logos and high-contrast headlines.
description: Chunk Chonk is an all-caps brutalist display typeface built around two distinct style families: Square, with rigid angular geometry, and Round, which softens the same block structures with curved terminals. Each family runs Regular, Bold and Black. With only 68 glyphs and no lowercase, its use is narrow – blunt, single-word headlines, logo lockups and packaging where weight is the point.
foundry_blurb: Ultra-thick letterforms and powerful block structures across Square and Round families, each combining rigid geometry with softer curves. Designed for logos, streetwear branding, posters, packaging and any project where typography needs to feel strong and instantly recognisable.

name: Crud
classification_notes: Retro pixel display typeface with two distinct visual variants – Square and Round – each offered in Regular and Bold. Deliberately rough, low-resolution aesthetic referencing early digital graphics and vintage computing.
summary: A deliberately rough retro pixel typeface by Jason Santos, available in Square and Round variants for gaming visuals, posters and experimental branding.
description: Crud is a pixel display typeface designed by Jason Santos, drawing from early digital graphics and vintage computing culture. It comes in two visual subfamilies – Square and Round – each with Regular and Bold weights, totalling four styles. The intentionally coarse, low-resolution character suits gaming visuals, album artwork, apparel graphics and logo work, though its novelty limits it to decorative use.
foundry_blurb: Crud captures the imperfect character of early digital graphics through a retro pixel aesthetic. Square and Round subfamilies each come in Regular and Bold, covering posters, logos, album art, apparel and UI concepts. Available in OTF and TTF (with WOFF and WOFF2 on the extended licence).

name: Lanky
classification_notes: Ultra-tall, narrow display typeface with extreme vertical proportions. Two subfamilies — Square (angular) and Round (softer curves) — each in three weights. Limited to 94 glyphs covering basic Latin; no diacritics indicated.
summary: A geometric display typeface built on extreme vertical proportions, offered in Square and Round subfamilies across three weights.
description: Lanky is an ultra-tall display typeface with narrow, elongated letterforms designed for large-scale headline and branding work. Two subfamilies — Square and Round — offer a choice between angular construction and softer curves, each in Regular, Bold and Black. The character set covers 94 glyphs, keeping it suited to short-form, high-impact typesetting rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: An ultra-tall display typeface built on extreme proportions and architectural structure. Available in Square and Round variants with narrow letterforms that create a distinctive rhythm, suited to modern branding, posters, fashion graphics and editorial headlines.

name: Dotter
classification_notes: Experimental display face constructed entirely from arranged dot patterns across four geometric style variants (Circles, Squares, Curvy, Geometric); no conventional weight range; inspired by matrix printing, halftone and digital screens; basic Latin coverage only.
summary: A dot-matrix display face by Jason Santos, built from arranged dot patterns across four geometric style variants and aimed at posters, branding and editorial work.
description: Dotter renders each glyph as graphic texture, constructing letterforms from systematically arranged dots in reference to matrix printing, halftone processes and digital screens. Four distinct variants – Circles, Squares, Curvy and Geometric – offer visual range within a single-trick concept. Coverage is basic Latin at 96 glyphs, limiting it to display and headline use in English-language contexts.
foundry_blurb: Dotter is an experimental textured display typeface built entirely from carefully arranged dots, drawing inspiration from matrix printing, digital screens and halftone processes. It comes in four variations – Circles, Squares, Curvy and Geometric – intended for posters, album covers, branding, editorial layouts, packaging and experimental typography projects. Supplied as OTF and TTF under a commercial licence.

name: Larva
classification_notes: All-caps experimental display face with sharp, angular forms inspired by futuristic monoliths. Prioritises visual cadence over legibility. 45-glyph character set, uppercase letters, numbers and basic punctuation only. No alternate weights, widths or italic styles.
summary: Larva is a near-illegible all-caps display face by Alex Ortiga, its sharp angular forms drawn from futuristic monolith aesthetics.
description: Designed as a visual rhythm system rather than a reading tool, Larva's 45-glyph uppercase-only set prioritises cadence over clarity. Sharp, angular shapes suit short headline treatments, cover type and experimental graphic work where atmosphere takes precedence over readability. Originally released through HIDE Productions in 2019 and available in OTF via commercial and extended licences.
foundry_blurb: Sharp and near-illegible by design, Larva takes its forms from futuristic monoliths. The intent is an aesthetic built on the cadence of the sign rather than the meaning of individual glyphs.
